# Home23 Worker Runtime + ShakedownJerry Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Repair the generic Home23 Worker runtime completely and deliver ShakedownJerry as Jerry's resident, production-operating worker for the full observe -> discover -> improve -> publish -> distribute -> convert -> learn -> recover loop.

**Architecture:** Jerry's existing Home23 harness owns lightweight per-worker runtimes. A strict manifest and signed standing grant resolve to an immutable execution profile; every request enters one authenticated durable SQLite/WAL queue; every consequential action crosses one `CapabilityExecutor.execute(envelope)` chokepoint; canonical receipts and destination-aware outboxes commit transactionally. ShakedownJerry uses typed deterministic adapters in the Shakedown repository, an independent pinned source clone, immutable code/site/data release journals, the existing Home23 Worker Desk, one Agency pursuit, and no separate engine, brain, dashboard, or PM2 family.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript/Node.js, Express, `better-sqlite3`, Ajv, YAML, Home23 `AgentLoop`/`ContextManager`/`ConversationHistory`, CommonJS Home23 engine modules, React/Vite, Bun, Supabase Auth/Postgres, Stripe, Matomo, Caddy, PM2, launchd, `node:test`, Playwright/browser acceptance, Ed25519 signatures, RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-21-shakedown-jerry-worker-runtime-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- This is one dependency-ordered delivery. A task may be completed and committed separately for review, but no task redefines a required capability as a later product version or optional parking-lot item.
- Reuse the already-existing clean `codex/shakedown-jerry-runtime` worktree at `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-worktrees/shakedown-jerry-runtime`; Task 1 inventories its lineage, brings in only this final plan commit, and freezes the partial auth/store worktrees. Do not recreate, reset, or clean any of them, and do not modify the user's dirty `main` worktree.
- Directory identity is exact: lowercase `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23` is the Home23 backend/control-plane repository used by this plan; uppercase `/Users/jtr/xCode_Builds/Home23` is the separate iOS/Apple client repository and is out of scope. Do not edit the uppercase tree; preserve its existing API/Bearer contracts through server compatibility tests.
- Preserve the existing Home23 modifications to `engine/src/realtime/websocket-server.js` and `src/home.ts` plus its untracked backup, verification, and receipt artifacts. Recheck the inventory before every integration.
- The Shakedown checkout at `/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com` is a dirty, 125-commit-ahead `velvet-sunset` worktree at baseline `2f0c8323ab1e1846360b070904f39181da8fe834`. Do not switch its branch, index it, clean it, reset it, build into its shared `shakedown-v2/dist`, or use it as the worker's editing environment.
- Establish the worker clone from the complete verified 15-commit acquisition/billing series `2f0c8323ab1e1846360b070904f39181da8fe834..4f0dbb926dd0ba5319e429f8820b2d28b5ea605a`, then reconcile captured local-only source as explicit three-way overlays. The cumulative range—not only the tip patch—must supply its Supabase migrations, Auth/account/checkout/Stripe/backend/frontend code, and tests before further Shakedown edits. A build from the stale `2f0c832` tree is forbidden.
- All Shakedown source edits happen in the independent clone at `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/shakedown-jerry/workspace/source-clones/shakedownshuffle`, on a dedicated worker branch. Integration may update only `refs/heads/codex/shakedown-worker/*` and must prove the active checkout's branch, HEAD, index, worktree inventory, and configured remotes are unchanged.
- The canonical mutable Worker root is `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers`, independent of immutable Home23 code releases and shared by the existing owner harnesses. Keep its directories mode `0700`, mutable files mode `0600`, snapshot/migrate it transactionally, and prove rollback/redeploy/restart preserve its SQLite, worker state, source clone, sessions, receipts, and activation records. Immutable code releases are read-only.
- The canonical mutable Shakedown data authority is `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/shakedown-runtime-data`, outside every source checkout and immutable code release. Backend releases, collection, and enrichment must resolve the same hash-pinned root; the current checkout-relative data is copied and hash-verified during migration, never deleted as part of cutover.
- Preservation artifacts live outside both repositories and worktrees at `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/preservation/shakedown-jerry-runtime`; public manifests are redacted, and restricted archives/dumps are mode `0600` beneath mode-`0700` directories and never enter Git, model context, or immutable public release artifacts.
- All frontend builds use a run-specific immutable output directory. Never write shared `shakedown-v2/dist`; Caddy serves it publicly as `v2.shakedownshuffle.com`.
- Do not edit `/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com/html` directly. Only the typed site publisher may snapshot, overlay candidate-controlled files, verify, cut over, and roll back. It must preserve and hash-check `html/pro`, `html/env-config.js`, and the complete live-only allowlist.
- Live/public capabilities remain disabled until an authenticated operator activates the exact signed `shakedown-jerry-standing` grant hash. That single activation removes per-action approval inside scope; machine preconditions remain mandatory.
- Tasks before standing-grant activation may use fixtures, isolated clones, ephemeral services, local candidates, and byte-equivalent staged release trees only. Real site cutover, public/channel action, production backend restart, live data promotion, and social-image publication occur only in Task 31 after activation; the payment lifecycle remains separately authorized in Task 32.
- A production signup/payment/entitlement canary requires a separate exact hard-stop authorization naming the owned identity, Supabase/Stripe/site targets, maximum amount, exact lifecycle and cleanup operations, expiry, immutable runner/catalog/root-module/leaf-router/operation-vocabulary/route-lock/state-machine hashes, cleanup plan, and redaction policy. Sandbox success is supporting evidence, not production proof.
- Database schema, Auth configuration, billing, entitlement, credential, account-ownership, DNS-account, destructive data, spend, and bulk-message changes remain hard stops. Read-only Supabase/Stripe observation does not grant mutation authority.
- Supabase project `pkbnsqnkuoifudvbbdbe` is the current `shakedown` project. Re-run official changelog/docs checks before implementation because Supabase interfaces change; keep exposed-table grants least-privilege, RLS enabled, and authorization owner-scoped. Never expose a service-role/secret key to a client, prompt, transcript, artifact, or receipt.
- Every worker action, including nested typed actions, re-enters `CapabilityExecutor.execute(envelope)`. Worker code may not call the generic `ToolRegistry.execute`, a deterministic adapter, shell, browser driver, database writer, or network client directly.
- Write `action_started` durably before side effects. Treat an uncertain consequential outcome as `reconciliation_required`; perform authoritative readback and never blindly repeat a post, send, promotion, cutover, or payment-adjacent action.
- The finite safety reserve is non-model, persistent across restart, and usable only for mandatory verifier/rollback steps after cutover. Exhaustion freezes only the affected target and creates an urgent Jerry-visible item.
- Preserve actual failure, denial, verifier, semantic, rollback, and consequence status in every projection. Raw transcripts never auto-promote to memory; only receipt-declared, verified `memoryCandidates` do.
- Keep the existing 120-second watchdog as the deterministic `jerry-api` recovery owner, keep `ops/dynamic-dns` independent and outside the grant, and keep Jerry Collection Manager/action-worker definitions until consequence parity is live-proven.
- Do not delete or retire any current automation before replacement consequence parity is live-proven. A bounded cutover may pause the exact legacy ingresses only after the disabled replacement has passed fixture/read-only shadow and restart reconstruction, the complete inverse definitions are journaled, and all consequential lanes are fenced; the shared data/backend/frontend cutover and explicit activation-epoch replacement canaries must then pass before the pause becomes the completed state. Any failure follows the phase-aware recovery rules in Tasks 22 and 31; definitions and historical receipts are never deleted.
- Commit after each green task with only that task's intended files. Never stage or commit unrelated user-owned changes.
- Every command runs from either `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-worktrees/shakedown-jerry-runtime` or the absolute Shakedown clone root above. Use `git -C` or an explicit subshell for every cross-repository command; never rely on a previous `cd` carrying into the next step.

## File Structure

### Home23 — create

- `src/workers/schema.ts` — strict v1/v2 manifest and receipt validators plus compatibility translation.
- `src/workers/principal.ts` — immutable worker-management principals and operation scopes.
- `src/workers/auth.ts` — fail-closed Express authentication/authorization middleware.
- `src/workers/grants.ts` — Ed25519/RFC-8785 grant verification, precedence, activation-state lookup, and action-time recheck.
- `src/workers/signing-keys.ts` — role-separated public-key registries plus Keychain-backed operator-signing and automated-dispatch operations.
- `src/workers/macos-keychain.ts` and `native/worker-keychain-helper.swift` — the real non-shelling Security.framework adapter used by production key commands; the in-memory store is test-only.
- `src/workers/credential-authorities.ts` — closed non-secret credential-authority registry plus operator-only Keychain inventory/provision/validate/rotate workflows.
- `src/workers/hard-stop-authorizations.ts` — exact-hash, expiring, bounded, non-standing authorization validation.
- `src/workers/profile.ts` — immutable `WorkerExecutionProfile` resolution and deep freezing.
- `src/workers/store.ts` — SQLite/WAL migrations and transactional requests, attempts, leases, locks, actions, journals, receipts, activation records, outbox, and event cursors.
- `src/workers/state.ts` — canonical opportunity/campaign/channel/action state APIs and atomic filesystem projections.
- `src/workers/dispatcher.ts` — enqueue, atomic claim, lease heartbeat/reclaim, retry, cancel, capacity, and startup reconciliation.
- `src/workers/runtime.ts` — per-attempt worker-specific loop/context/history/tool/brain construction.
- `src/workers/runtime-factory.ts` — concrete provider/model/credential-authority resolution at claim.
- `src/workers/budget.ts` — cumulative token/tool/runtime/artifact/retry budgets and finite safety reserve.
- `src/workers/brain-delegate.ts` — owner plus worker principal, scoped reads, and verified-candidate promotion.
- `src/workers/capabilities/types.ts` — action envelope, normalized targets, decisions, adapter contracts, and structured events.
- `src/workers/capabilities/executor.ts` — the sole action chokepoint.
- `src/workers/capabilities/registry.ts` — explicit capability definitions and filtered worker tool registry.
- `src/workers/network-policies.ts` — typed closed request builders/validators compiled from one versioned network-policy authority.
- `src/workers/capabilities/shakedown-adapter.ts` — fixed subprocess bridge from `CapabilityExecutor` to an immutable Shakedown runner release.
- `src/workers/adapter-dispatch.ts` — short-lived signed parent-action envelope and cancellation/progress transport.
- `src/workers/outbox.ts` — destination-aware delivery with acknowledgement, retry, and idempotency.
- `src/workers/projections.ts` — atomic filesystem receipt, audit feed, dashboard, and memory projections.
- `src/workers/client.ts` — the single authenticated management/dispatch client used by in-process callers.

The existing unversioned `WorkerRunStatus`, `WorkerVerifierStatus`, `WorkerConfig`, `WorkerRunRequest`, `WorkerRunReceipt`, connector events, runner, registry, CLI, and dashboard consumers remain source-compatible in this task. Add strict semantics only under the explicit `WorkerRunStatusV2`, `WorkerVerifierStatusV2`, `WorkerLimitsV2`, `WorkerResourceUseV2`, `WorkerSemanticStatusV2`, and nested `*V2` names. Export them from `src/workers/index.ts` with the repository's NodeNext `.js` import convention. Task 15 owns installed-manifest migration and later runtime tasks adopt v2 deliberately.

Remove caller-owned `ownerAgent`, `requestedBy`, `requester`, visibility, grant identity, source identity, authorization hash, authority source, and authorization summary from the public run body. An authenticated operator endpoint may accept a selected hash only to resolve an already registered authorization; it verifies the exact document and approval receipt, then persists the resulting `TrustedHardStopBinding` inside the trusted request. `receiptId` is mandatory in every v2 receipt and is the one canonical cross-system receipt identity: `deriveWorkerReceiptId()` hashes only the exact `{ schema, ownerAgent, worker, runId, requestId }` identity tuple above. Ajv validation and `decodeWorkerReceipt()` recompute it and reject a mismatched or independently invented ID; every v2 fixture, outbox payload, scheduler consequence, event causation link, Agency consequence, and dashboard receipt URL uses that field. The SHA-256 of the complete canonical receipt bytes remains the separate content-integrity identity and is never substituted for `receiptId`. `authorityGrantHash` is mandatory in every decoded receipt: v2 uses the exact signed standing-grant hash, while a decoded legacy receipt uses the SHA-256 hash of the effective compatibility/authority policy produced by the named legacy translation map. A hard-stop run additionally records `hardStopAuthorizationHash` in its receipt and every consequential action evidence row. Define each nested v2 receipt and hard-stop schema with `additionalProperties: false`; every Checkout field above is required, the host/callback arrays are sorted unique HTTPS authorities, and their hashes must equal canonical array hashes. `privateIdentityBindings` is a sorted exact four-record set whose aliases must equal the four dedicated alias fields. Preparation resolves immutable private-record descriptors, versions, and a stable Keychain persistent-reference identity, computes each non-reversible fingerprint with a separate Keychain HMAC key, and signs the canonical set and hash; it never hashes a raw low-entropy email without the HMAC or emits secret bytes. Browser cookies and derived OAuth access tokens are excluded from the immutable descriptors; the bound descriptor names the fixed profile/account/credential authority whose mutable session material stays private. Nested receipt types include exact action target/policy/redacted-input/result/rollback fields; evidence source/freshness/hash/verifier fields; artifact URI/hash/media-type/role fields; and provenance/confidence/destination for every memory candidate. A hard-stop authorization is signed, exact, expiring, non-standing, bounded to one canonical orchestration plan, capability state machine, immutable runner/catalog/root-module/leaf-router/mailbox adapter dependency closure/private checkout contract/idempotency derivation/session-journal schema, operation vocabulary, disjoint route-lock policy, fresh private identity bindings, exact product/price/amount/currency, Checkout host/callback and signup-confirmation sets, exact Supabase/Stripe/site/mailbox targets, cleanup plan/safety policy, and redaction policy, and never represented as a standing-grant capability. `BILLING_CANARY_OPERATIONS` and `BILLING_CANARY_CLEANUP_OPERATIONS` are the sole TypeScript and Ajv enum sources used by preparation, signing, verification, reservation, routing, CLI validation, and tests. The cleanup safety vocabulary exactly overlaps main operations at `cancel`, `refund`, and `cleanup` and adds safety-only `expire-session`; the cleanup set is not required to be a subset of the main set, and no other operation can use the safety lane. Guest pending activation remains a separately tested backend path and is deliberately absent from this authenticated canary vocabulary.

`src/workers/schema.ts` must reject unknown v2 fields, invalid limits, unknown capabilities, contradictory policies, invalid history/concurrency combinations, empty write scopes, and invalid relative prompt references. Legacy tools become the intersection of manifest intent and a named compatibility map; current accidental full-registry authority is never preserved.

```ts
const LEGACY_TOOL_CAPABILITIES: Readonly<Record<string, readonly WorkerCapabilityId[]>> = Object.freeze({
  shell: ['home23.observe', 'home23.verify'],
  files: ['home23.observe'],
  cron: ['home23.observe'],
  brain: ['home23.observe'],
  web: ['home23.observe'],
});

const workerManifestV2Schema = {
  $id: 'home23.worker.v2',
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: [
    'schema', 'kind', 'name', 'displayName', 'ownerAgent', 'class', 'purpose',
    'provider', 'model', 'context', 'capabilities', 'hardStopCapabilities', 'authorityGrant', 'paths',
    'limits', 'safetyReserve', 'retry', 'feedsBrains', 'visibleTo',
  ],
  properties: {
    schema: { const: 'home23.worker.v2' },
    kind: { const: 'worker' },
    name: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$' },
    displayName: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    ownerAgent: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    class: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    purpose: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    provider: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    model: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    context: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['promptRoots', 'identityFiles', 'sessionHistory', 'ownerBrainRead'],
      properties: {
        promptRoots: { type: 'array', minItems: 1, uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
        identityFiles: { type: 'array', minItems: 4, maxItems: 4, uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
        sessionHistory: { enum: ['fresh', 'persistent'] },
        ownerBrainRead: {
          type: 'array',
          items: {
            type: 'object',
            additionalProperties: false,
            required: ['agent', 'scopes'],
            properties: {
              agent: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
              scopes: { type: 'array', uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
    capabilities: { type: 'array', uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
    hardStopCapabilities: { type: 'array', uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
    authorityGrant: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
    paths: { $ref: '#/$defs/paths' },
    limits: { $ref: '#/$defs/limits' },
    safetyReserve: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['maxRuntimeMinutes', 'maxToolCalls', 'maxArtifactBytes', 'retryAttempts'],
      properties: {
        maxRuntimeMinutes: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
        maxToolCalls: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
        maxArtifactBytes: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
        retryAttempts: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
      },
    },
    retry: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['transientAttempts', 'initialBackoffSeconds', 'maxBackoffSeconds'],
      properties: {
        transientAttempts: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
        initialBackoffSeconds: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
        maxBackoffSeconds: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
      },
    },
    feedsBrains: { type: 'array', uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
    visibleTo: { type: 'array', minItems: 1, uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
  },
  $defs: {
    pathList: { type: 'array', uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
    paths: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['read', 'write', 'artifact'],
      properties: {
        read: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        write: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        sourceClone: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        gitMetadata: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        codeRelease: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        runtimeWrite: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        dataWrite: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        quarantine: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        collectionCandidate: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        collectionStash: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        artifact: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        privateRead: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        receipt: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        releaseCandidate: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
        liveWebroot: { $ref: '#/$defs/pathList' },
      },
    },
    limits: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['maxRuntimeMinutes', 'maxToolCalls', 'maxTokens', 'maxArtifactBytes', 'maxConcurrentRuns'],
      properties: {
        maxRuntimeMinutes: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
        maxToolCalls: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
        maxConcurrentRuns: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 8 },
        maxTokens: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
        maxArtifactBytes: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
      },
    },
  },
} as const;

export function parseWorkerManifest(input: unknown): WorkerManifestV2 {
  const candidate = translateLegacyManifest(input, LEGACY_TOOL_CAPABILITIES);
  if (!validateWorkerManifestV2(candidate)) {
    throw new WorkerSchemaError(validateWorkerManifestV2.errors ?? []);
  }
  assertKnownCapabilities(candidate.capabilities);
  assertKnownHardStopCapabilities(candidate.hardStopCapabilities);
  assertDisjointCapabilityLanes(candidate.capabilities, candidate.hardStopCapabilities);
  assertEffectiveWriteScopes(candidate);
  assertConfinedPromptReferences(candidate);
  return structuredClone(candidate);
}
```

The legacy translator always materializes `hardStopCapabilities: []`; compatibility input can never acquire a hard-stop ceiling. Ajv builds both hard-stop operation enums directly from the two frozen constants above and rejects duplicates, unknown operations, and any order other than the frozen order. It validates main operations and cleanup-safety operations independently: `expire-session` is safety-only and therefore must not appear in `allowedOperations`; `cancel`, `refund`, and `cleanup` must appear in both lists. Guest `pending-state-reconcile` remains outside this authenticated canary vocabulary. The resulting combined sequence must satisfy the fixed billing state machine without imposing an impossible cleanup-subset rule.

Move `ajv` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` and update `package-lock.json`; strict manifest/action/receipt parsing is production runtime code. Add a production-install test that runs `npm ci --omit=dev` in an isolated copy and boots the schema parser without ancestor dependency resolution.

Validate official RFC vectors, reject lone surrogates/non-JSON values, and distinguish the unsigned payload hash from the exact signed-document hash used by activation. Validate identity, validity window, operator-authority key role, capabilities as a subset of `manifest.capabilities` only, zero intersection with `manifest.hardStopCapabilities`, narrower path/account/host/action scopes, hard denies, and the separately injected exact-hash activation lookup. Signature verification remains pure; Task 5 supplies durable activation state. Deep-freeze the resolved profile.

Resolve the symbolic `worker-workspace` root through a closed alias map to `<workerRoot>/workspace`. Open every prompt with no-follow semantics, verify stable device/inode/size/mtime before and after reading, confine it to the resolved workspace, and pin SHA-256. Bind immutable `IDENTITY.md` and `PLAYBOOK.md` in the standing grant; pin all four prompt files in the per-attempt profile and recheck all four on resume, because `NOW.md` and `MEMORY.md` are mutable receipt projections.
```ts
export interface WorkerExecutionProfile {
  worker: string;
  ownerAgent: string;
  manifestHash: string;
  authorityGrantHash: string;
  provider: string;
  model: string;
  credentialAuthorityId: string;
  workerRoot: string;
  workspaceRoot: string;
  history: 'fresh' | 'persistent';
  brainReadScopes: readonly string[];
  capabilities: readonly string[];
  hardStopCapabilities: readonly string[];
  promptDocuments: readonly Array<{ path: string; sha256: string }>;
  collectionConfigHash?: string;
  collectionTargets: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  limits: Readonly<WorkerLimitsV2>;
  authority: Readonly<WorkerEffectiveAuthority>;
  collectionAvailability: Readonly<WorkerCollectionAvailability>;
}

export async function resolveWorkerExecutionProfile(
  input: ResolveWorkerExecutionProfileInput,
): Promise<Readonly<WorkerExecutionProfile>> {
  const manifest = parseWorkerManifest(await readYaml(input.manifestPath));
  const verifiedGrant = await verifyWorkerGrant(await readYaml(input.grantPath), input.publicKeys);
  assertGrantIsManifestSubset(verifiedGrant, manifest);
  assertStandingGrantExcludesHardStopCapabilities(verifiedGrant, manifest.hardStopCapabilities);
  const promptDocuments = await Promise.all(
    manifest.context.identityFiles.map((path) => resolveConfinedPromptStable({
      workerRoot: input.workerRoot,
      promptRootAliases: { 'worker-workspace': 'workspace' },
      promptRoots: manifest.context.promptRoots,
      path,
    })),
  );
  const concreteProvider = resolveOwnerProviderTuple(manifest, input.ownerDefaults);
  const collection = await resolvePinnedCollectionConfig(input.collectionConfigPath, verifiedGrant);
  const standingCapabilities = intersectCapabilities(manifest.capabilities, verifiedGrant.capabilities);
  const capabilities = collection && !collection.availability.writeAllowed
    ? narrowCapabilitiesForCollectionDegradation(standingCapabilities, {
        preserve: ['shakedown.observe'],
        removePrefixes: ['shakedown.collection.'],
      })
    : standingCapabilities;
  return deepFreeze({
    worker: manifest.name,
    ownerAgent: manifest.ownerAgent,
    manifestHash: sha256Canonical(manifest),
    authorityGrantHash: verifiedGrant.documentHash,
    provider: concreteProvider.provider,
    model: concreteProvider.model,
    credentialAuthorityId: input.credentialAuthorityId,
    workerRoot: await realpath(input.workerRoot),
    workspaceRoot: await realpath(join(input.workerRoot, 'workspace')),
    history: manifest.context.sessionHistory,
    brainReadScopes: intersectBrainReadScopes(
      manifest.context.ownerBrainRead.flatMap((read) => read.scopes),
      verifiedGrant.brainReadScopes,
    ),
    capabilities,
    hardStopCapabilities: resolveRegisteredHardStopCapabilities(manifest.hardStopCapabilities),
    promptDocuments,
    collectionConfigHash: collection?.configHash,
    collectionTargets: collection?.targets ?? {},
    collectionAvailability: collection?.availability ?? { writeAllowed: false, reason: 'not_configured' },
    limits: narrowLimits(manifest.limits, verifiedGrant.limits),
    authority: resolveEffectiveAuthority(verifiedGrant),
  });
}
```

The strict grant schema/finalizer must carry the fields consumed here: `brainReadScopes`, `limits`, effective path/service/host/account/action-class scopes, hard denies, rate policy, communications policy, immutable prompt hashes, collection config hash, and collection target hash. Verify both collection hashes. Keep these effective scopes in the immutable profile, or load and reverify the exact same signed document at action time; never reconstruct them from the manifest alone. Load YAML using `js-yaml` `JSON_SCHEMA` so ISO strings cannot silently become `Date` objects.

`hardStopCapabilities` is a declaration ceiling, not effective standing authority. It is hash-bound into the profile and immutable runner catalog, but it is excluded from `capabilities`, excluded from every standing-grant intersection, and absent from the normal model tool registry. Task 6 may expose one of these definitions for a run only when the trusted stored request carries a server-resolved active exact hard-stop authorization hash for that same principal/capability; every action-time check can only narrow or revoke it. The six built-in v2 templates and every legacy translation explicitly set `hardStopCapabilities: []`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the real Ed25519 key authority and CLI**

`src/workers/signing-keys.ts` loads installation-specific public records from the stable already-ignored Worker state path `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/worker-signing-keys.json`, whose portable shape is tracked only as `config/worker-signing-keys.json.example`. The path is resolved through the typed Worker runtime root, not through the immutable code release or the original checkout's `config/` directory. Private operator authority uses macOS Keychain service `com.jtr.home23.worker-grants`; runtime dispatch uses the distinct `com.jtr.home23.worker-dispatch` service and a distinct key role/ID. The resident runtime can access only the dispatch signer and can never sign a standing grant or hard-stop authorization.

`src/workers/macos-keychain.ts` is the required production `KeychainPrivateKeyStore`; the in-memory implementation is test-only and production CLI construction rejects it. The adapter launches only the immutable, hash-verified `native/worker-keychain-helper` with `shell: false`, a closed operation enum, fixed service/role/key-ID arguments, a minimal environment, and framed stdin/stdout. `native/worker-keychain-helper.swift` uses macOS Security.framework directly for generate/import/public-key/sign/has-key operations, binds each non-exportable Ed25519 key to its exact Keychain service/account/access group, and emits only public SPKI, signature, persistent-reference identity, and typed status. Private import bytes travel only in the helper's stdin frame, are zeroed after `SecItemAdd`, and never appear in argv, environment, stdout, error strings, receipts, or the public registry. The helper rejects service/role substitution and duplicate/mismatched public records. Its binary path and SHA-256 are bound into the immutable release manifest and Task 29 boot proof.

`home23 worker key init`, `key import`, `key rotate`, and `grant sign` are platform-gated and construct that real adapter in production; dependency injection may substitute a fake only in tests. A permissioned-file import accepts only an explicit stable, owner-matched, non-symlink regular file at mode `0600`, imports without exposing key bytes in argv/stdout, then securely removes or returns the still-confined source according to an explicit option. Signing constructs `signingKeyId` and `signatureAlgorithm` in the unsigned payload first, canonicalizes second, refuses an already-active or target-drifted policy, writes no private material, and emits a mode-`0600` hash-only receipt beneath a caller-supplied fixture receipt root. Unit tests use a fake store; a macOS-only integration test compiles the helper, creates an isolated temporary test keychain, exercises generate/public/sign/role-denial/import without the user's login keychain, deletes only that test-created keychain, and scans process arguments, Git, config, and artifacts for private material.

```ts
export function createMacOSKeychainPrivateKeyStore(input: {
  helperPath: string;
  helperSha256: string;
  services: Readonly<Record<'operator-authority' | 'runtime-dispatch', string>>;
  keychainPath?: string;
}): KeychainPrivateKeyStore & { readonly kind: 'macos-keychain' };
```

`home23 worker grant finalize <grant> --write` is the only mutating hash-finalization command. It loads the named grant-shaped document with YAML `JSON_SCHEMA`, resolves its worker manifest, immutable prompt files, collection configuration and target map, channel registry, event bindings, immutable adapter-runner release, exact path/service/host/account targets, policies, and hard denies. It intersects capabilities/scopes/limits with the manifest and candidate, rejects broadening, populates missing initial timestamps only once, recomputes every bound SHA-256 value, removes any invalidated signature, writes atomically only with `--write`, and prints both the unsigned payload hash and—when signed—the exact signed-document hash. Resolution, signing, and rename operate under one lock with stable before/after snapshots of every bound input; drift aborts before replacement. `--output <final-grant>` is permitted only when the input resolves beneath `config/worker-authority-grants/candidates/` and the output is either the exact fixture sibling authority root or the named worker's explicit confined installation-local `instances/workers/<worker>/authority/` root; it writes the complete finalized policy atomically, so an incomplete document never appears at a loadable path. Without `--write` it is a byte-preserving dry run. `grant validate-candidate` accepts an incomplete unsigned document only beneath the ignored `candidates/` directory; `grant verify --scope-ceiling <candidate>` is read-only and rejects missing final fields, scope broadening, a bad signature, or a mutable activation field. Task 29 calls the same finalizer in place before `grant sign`.

```ts
export interface WorkerSigningKeyAuthority {
  generate(keyId: string): Promise<WorkerPublicKeyRecord>;
  importPrivateKey(
    keyId: string,
    sourcePath: string,
    options?: { removeSource: boolean },
  ): Promise<WorkerPublicKeyRecord>;
  rotate(currentKeyId: string, nextKeyId: string): Promise<WorkerPublicKeyRecord>;
  sign<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(
    kind: 'standing-grant' | 'hard-stop-authorization' | 'adapter-invocation',
    keyId: string,
    document: T,
  ): Promise<T & SignedFields>;
}

const ALLOWED_SIGNING_KINDS = Object.freeze({
  'operator-authority': new Set(['standing-grant', 'hard-stop-authorization']),
  'runtime-dispatch': new Set(['adapter-invocation']),
} as const);

export function createSigningKeyAuthority(input: {
  keychain: KeychainPrivateKeyStore;
  publicRegistry: WorkerPublicKeyRegistryStore;
  role: WorkerSigningKeyRole;
  isDocumentActive?: (document: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>) => boolean | Promise<boolean>;
  assertDocumentTargetsCurrent?: (document: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>) => void | Promise<void>;
}): WorkerSigningKeyAuthority {
  if (!['operator-authority', 'runtime-dispatch'].includes(input.role)) {
    throw new Error(`Unknown worker signing role: ${String(input.role)}`);
  }

  async function register(keyId: string, generated: GeneratedPublicKey): Promise<WorkerPublicKeyRecord> {
    const record = publicRecord(keyId, input.role, generated);
    await input.publicRegistry.put(record);
    return record;
  }

  return {
    async generate(keyId) {
      assertKeyId(keyId);
      if (await input.publicRegistry.get(keyId)) throw new Error(`Worker public key already exists: ${keyId}`);
      if (await input.keychain.hasPrivateKey(keyId)) {
        return register(keyId, await input.keychain.getPublicKey(keyId, input.role));
      }
      return register(keyId, await input.keychain.generateEd25519(keyId, input.role));
    },
    async importPrivateKey(keyId, sourcePath, options = { removeSource: false }) {
      assertKeyId(keyId);
      if (await input.publicRegistry.get(keyId)) throw new Error(`Worker public key already exists: ${keyId}`);
      const stable = assertStablePrivateKeySource(sourcePath);
      try {
        let generated: GeneratedPublicKey;
        if (await input.keychain.hasPrivateKey(keyId)) {
          generated = await input.keychain.getPublicKey(keyId, input.role);
          const sourceKey = createPrivateKey(stable.bytes);
          if (sourceKey.asymmetricKeyType !== 'ed25519'
            || spkiBase64(sourceKey) !== generated.publicKey) {
            throw new Error(`Private signing key import retry does not match orphaned key: ${keyId}`);
          }
        } else {
          generated = await input.keychain.importEd25519(keyId, input.role, stable.bytes);
        }
        const record = await register(keyId, generated);
        if (options.removeSource) securelyRemoveImportedSource(sourcePath, stable);
        return record;
      } finally {
        stable.bytes.fill(0);
        closeSync(stable.fd);
      }
    },
    async rotate(currentKeyId, nextKeyId) {
      await input.publicRegistry.requireExactRole(currentKeyId, input.role);
      if (!(await input.keychain.hasPrivateKey(currentKeyId))) {
        throw new Error(`Current private signing key not available: ${currentKeyId}`);
      }
      return this.generate(nextKeyId);
    },
    async sign(kind, keyId, document) {
      if (!ALLOWED_SIGNING_KINDS[input.role].has(kind)) {
        throw new WorkerSigningRoleError(input.role, kind);
      }
      assertKeyId(keyId);
      await input.publicRegistry.requireExactRole(keyId, input.role);
      if (!(await input.keychain.hasPrivateKey(keyId))) {
        throw new Error(`Private signing key unavailable in ${WORKER_KEYCHAIN_SERVICES[input.role]}: ${keyId}`);
      }
      if (input.isDocumentActive && await input.isDocumentActive(document)) {
        throw new Error('Refusing to sign an already-active Worker policy');
      }
      if (kind !== 'adapter-invocation' && !input.assertDocumentTargetsCurrent) {
        throw new Error('Worker policy signing requires a target-current verifier');
      }
      if (input.assertDocumentTargetsCurrent) await input.assertDocumentTargetsCurrent(document);
      const unsigned = { ...document, signingKeyId: keyId, signatureAlgorithm: 'Ed25519' as const };
      const signature = await input.keychain.signEd25519(keyId, canonicalJsonBytes(unsigned));
      return { ...unsigned, signature: signature.toString('base64') } as T & SignedFields;
    },
  };
}

export async function finalizeWorkerGrant(
  grantPath: string,
  options: {
    write: boolean;
    outputPath?: string;
    workerAuthorityRoot?: string;
    resolver: WorkerGrantBindingResolver;
    now: () => Date;
  },
): Promise<{ grantHash: string; changed: boolean; document: WorkerGrantDocument }> {
  const originalBytes = await readFile(grantPath);
  const candidateInput = isConfinedGrantCandidatePath(grantPath);
  const original = parseGrantCandidateOrFinalYaml(originalBytes, { allowIncomplete: candidateInput });
  const destinationPath = resolveFinalizedGrantDestination({
    grantPath, outputPath: options.outputPath, candidateInput,
    workerAuthorityRoot: options.workerAuthorityRoot,
  });
  const bindings = await options.resolver.resolveAll(workerNameFromPrincipal(original.principal));
  const finalizedAt = original.issuedAt ?? options.now().toISOString();
  const document = withoutSignature({
    schema: 'home23.worker-authority-grant.v1',
    id: original.id,
    version: original.version,
    principal: original.principal,
    ownerAgent: original.ownerAgent,
    issuedAt: finalizedAt,
    notBefore: original.notBefore ?? finalizedAt,
    expiresAt: original.expiresAt ?? null,
    signatureAlgorithm: 'Ed25519',
    signingKeyId: original.signingKeyId,
    capabilities: intersectAndRequireCandidateCapabilities(original.capabilities, bindings.manifestCapabilities),
    brainReadScopes: intersectScopes(original.brainReadScopes, bindings.manifestBrainReadScopes),
    limits: narrowLimits(bindings.manifestLimits, original.limits),
    pathScopes: bindings.pathScopes,
    serviceTargets: bindings.serviceTargets,
    hostTargets: bindings.hostTargets,
    accountTargets: bindings.accountTargets,
    actionClasses: original.actionClasses,
    ratePolicy: bindings.ratePolicy,
    communicationPolicy: bindings.communicationPolicy,
    hardDenies: requireNonOverridableHardDenies(original.hardDenies),
    manifestHash: bindings.manifestHash,
    immutablePromptHashes: bindings.immutablePromptHashes,
    collectionConfigHash: bindings.collectionConfigHash,
    collectionTargetHash: bindings.collectionTargetHash,
    channelRegistryHash: bindings.channelRegistryHash,
    eventBindingsHash: bindings.eventBindingsHash,
    adapterRunnerReleaseHash: bindings.adapterRunnerReleaseHash,
  });
  assertNoScopeBroadening({ candidate: original, manifest: bindings.manifest, finalized: document });
  const unsignedPayloadChanged = sha256Canonical(withoutSignature(original)) !== sha256Canonical(document);
  const signatureStillValid = Boolean(original.signature) && await verifyGrantDocumentSignature(original);
  const outputDocument = !unsignedPayloadChanged && signatureStillValid
    ? { ...document, signature: original.signature }
    : document;
  if (!unsignedPayloadChanged && signatureStillValid && destinationPath === grantPath) {
    return { grantHash: sha256CanonicalSignedDocument(original), changed: false, document: original };
  }
  const serialized = serializeCanonicalYaml(outputDocument);
  const currentDestinationBytes = await readFileIfExists(destinationPath);
  const changed = !currentDestinationBytes?.equals(Buffer.from(serialized, 'utf8'));
  if (options.write && changed) await writeFileAtomic(destinationPath, serialized, 0o600);
  return { grantHash: sha256CanonicalSignedDocument(outputDocument), changed, document: outputDocument };
}
```

Core tests use `tests/fixtures/workers/jerry-collection-config.json`; they never depend on the ignored local `/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com/ops/jerry-collection/config.json`. An opt-in local conformance test may compare that canonical installation when present without mutating it. Unknown keys, target drift, missing target volume, or a changed hash narrow the profile to observation and return `require-human-authorization` for collection writes until a newly signed grant is activated; they do not make read-only diagnosis unavailable.

```ts
const COLLECTION_PATH_KEYS = Object.freeze([
  'catalogPath', 'inventoryPath', 'sourceIndexPath', 'apiProjectionPath',
  'enrichmentRoot', 'normalizedDetailsPath', 'validationReportPath', 'unresolvedGapsPath',
  'reviewQueuePath', 'qualityReviewPath', 'sourceManifestPath', 'readableGuidePath',
  'newsletterIndexPath', 'runtimeDir', 'acquisitionQuarantineDir', 'releaseCandidateRoot',
  'stashRoot', 'collectionStatePath',
] as const);

const validateJerryCollectionConfig = new Ajv({ allErrors: true, strict: true }).compile({
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: [
    ...COLLECTION_PATH_KEYS, 'searchTargetVersion', 'enrichmentCommandIds',
    'playableValidation', 'operatorProductionActionsEnabled', 'timezone',
  ],
  properties: {
    ...Object.fromEntries(COLLECTION_PATH_KEYS.map((key) => [key, { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }])),
    searchTargetVersion: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
    enrichmentCommandIds: {
      type: 'array', minItems: 1, uniqueItems: true,
      items: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z0-9_]+$' },
    },
    playableValidation: {
      type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['minimumAudioFileCount', 'acceptedEvidence'],
      properties: {
        minimumAudioFileCount: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 },
        acceptedEvidence: { type: 'array', minItems: 1, uniqueItems: true, items: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 } },
      },
    },
    operatorProductionActionsEnabled: { type: 'boolean' },
    timezone: { const: 'America/New_York' },
  },
});

export async function resolvePinnedCollectionConfig(
  configPath: string | undefined,
  grant: VerifiedWorkerGrant,
): Promise<ResolvedCollectionConfig | undefined> {
  if (!configPath) return undefined;
  let bytes: Buffer;
  let config: unknown;
  try {
    bytes = await readFile(configPath);
    config = JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8'));
  } catch (error) {
    return degradedCollectionAuthority('collection config unavailable', error);
  }
  if (!validateJerryCollectionConfig(config)) {
    return degradedCollectionAuthority('invalid collection config', validateJerryCollectionConfig.errors);
  }
  const configHash = createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
  if (grant.collectionConfigHash !== configHash) return degradedCollectionAuthority('collection config hash drift');
  const parsed = config as JerryCollectionConfig;
  let targets: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  try {
    targets = Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(
      COLLECTION_PATH_KEYS.map(async (key) => [key, await resolveDeclaredPathSafely(parsed[key], {
        allowMissingLeaf: true, rejectSymlinkComponents: true, requireAbsolute: true,
      })]),
    )));
  } catch (error) {
    return degradedCollectionAuthority('collection target unavailable', error);
  }
  const targetHash = sha256Canonical(targets);
  if (grant.collectionTargetHash !== targetHash) return degradedCollectionAuthority('collection target hash drift');
  return { configHash, targetHash, targets, availability: { writeAllowed: true } };
}
```

This schema is the complete 23-key contract, not a parallel four-field approximation. The tracked Home23 fixture asserts all 23 keys/types and rejects each missing key, an unknown key, wrong scalar/nested type, relative path, unresolved volume, symlink component, and path escape. Task 22 may change only the intended path-key values and must pass this same validator before hashing; non-path policy fields remain byte-equivalent unless separately implemented and tested.

- [ ] **Step 6: Make registry loading isolated and visible**

One malformed worker must become a visible worker error without making every other worker disappear. Preserve the existing synchronous `listWorkers(projectRoot): WorkerConfig[]` contract used by today’s runner, connector, CLI, and tests. Add `scanWorkerRegistry(projectRoot): WorkerRegistryResult` for valid entries plus isolated validation errors. Make `loadWorker(projectRoot, name)` read the named directory directly so a malformed named worker reports its validation error instead of “not found”; reject directory/manifest-name mismatch, duplicate identity, and missing `worker.yaml`. Scaffold the established layout atomically and exclusively: `state`, `runs`, `logs`, and `locks` at worker root; `sessions` and `artifacts` beneath `workspace`. Preserve existing directories, use mode `0700` for directories and `0600` for mutable files, and refuse a partially occupied destination instead of overwriting it.

```ts
export async function scanWorkerRegistry(projectRoot: string): Promise<WorkerRegistryResult> {
  const root = workersDir(projectRoot);
  const entries = await readdir(root, { withFileTypes: true });
  const workers: WorkerRegistryEntry[] = [];
  const errors: WorkerRegistryError[] = [];
  for (const entry of entries.filter((row) => row.isDirectory()).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
    try {
      workers.push(await loadWorker(projectRoot, entry.name));
    } catch (error) {
      errors.push({ worker: entry.name, message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
    }
  }
  return { workers, errors };
}

export async function scaffoldWorker(root: string, worker: string): Promise<void> {
  for (const directory of ['state', 'runs', 'logs', 'locks', 'workspace/sessions', 'workspace/artifacts']) {
    await mkdir(join(root, worker, directory), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  }
}
```

The exact internal subjects are `service:scheduler:jerry`, `service:event-router:jerry`, `service:agency:jerry`, `service:good-life:jerry`, `service:live-problems:jerry`, and `service:payment-settlement-observer:jerry`; aliases or a generic `service:jerry` subject are unknown. A closed server registry keyed by exact `sub` binds `kind`, owner, sorted unique catalog-derived scopes, trigger, credential ID/generation, `operationCatalogHash`, and `authenticatedSourceRef`; none is inferred from a generic kind or body. `issue()` accepts only `subject` and `expiresAt`, resolves every other claim from that registry, and uses the injected clock. Verification re-resolves the row and requires every signed claim and current catalog hash to match before returning a deep-frozen clone. Keep the file valid CommonJS only (`'use strict'`, `require`, `module.exports`); no `import` or `export` token is legal in a `.cjs` implementation or generated fixture.

The live root is a dedicated strong Keychain-backed secret available only to the owner harness servers. It is never `BRIDGE_TOKEN`, Git, argv, receipts, `commonEnv`, engine, dashboard, MCP, browser, or public-site state. Client issuance derives a subject/generation key; a client cannot choose or derive another subject. `cli/lib/generate-ecosystem.js` carries only closed service/account references and principal IDs through allowlisted environment plumbing. Mounting and client migration are atomic: Home23 tools, Live Problems, CLI, dashboard, scheduler, event router, Agency, Good Life, and settlement observer each use their own fresh scoped issuer, never the unrelated harness-notify token or a browser bearer. Missing/malformed root or any enabled-client record leaves the router unavailable with `503`; there is no unauthenticated compatibility route.

```js
'use strict';

const { WORKER_OPERATION_SCOPES, WORKER_MANAGEMENT_OPERATION_CATALOG_HASH } =
  require('./worker-management-catalog.cjs');
const WORKER_CREDENTIAL_DOMAIN = 'home23.worker-management.credential.v1';
const WORKER_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE = 'home23.worker-management.v1';
const MAX_CREDENTIAL_BYTES = 4096;
const MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2048;
const MAX_TTL_MS = 300_000;
const CLAIM_FIELDS = Object.freeze([
  'v', 'aud', 'sub', 'kind', 'ownerAgent', 'scopes', 'trigger',
  'credentialId', 'generation', 'operationCatalogHash',
  'authenticatedSourceRef', 'issuedAt', 'expiresAt',
]);

function createWorkerCredentialAuthority(options) {
  assertExactAuthorityOptions(options);
  assertStrongRootSecret(options.rootSecret);
  const registry = validateAndFreezePrincipalRegistry(options.principalRegistry, WORKER_OPERATION_SCOPES);
  const now = options.now ?? Date.now;

  function issue(input) {
    assertExactKeys(input, ['subject', 'expiresAt']);
    const registered = requireRegisteredPrincipal(registry, input.subject);
    const issuedAt = canonicalNow(now);
    assertCanonicalPositiveBoundedTtl(issuedAt, input.expiresAt, MAX_TTL_MS);
    const claims = claimsFromRegisteredPrincipal(registered, {
      aud: WORKER_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE,
      operationCatalogHash: WORKER_MANAGEMENT_OPERATION_CATALOG_HASH,
      issuedAt,
      expiresAt: input.expiresAt,
    });
    const payloadBytes = canonicalCredentialBytes(claims, MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES);
    const key = deriveSubjectGenerationKey(options.rootSecret, registered, WORKER_CREDENTIAL_DOMAIN);
    return encodeCanonicalCredential(
      payloadBytes, signDomainSeparated(payloadBytes, key), MAX_CREDENTIAL_BYTES,
    );
  }

  function verify(token, expected) {
    assertExactKeys(expected, ['requiredScope']);
    assertClosedWorkerScope(expected.requiredScope, WORKER_OPERATION_SCOPES);
    const decoded = decodeCanonicalCredential(token, {
      maximumTokenBytes: MAX_CREDENTIAL_BYTES, maximumPayloadBytes: MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES,
    });
    const claims = parseExactCanonicalClaims(decoded.payloadBytes, CLAIM_FIELDS);
    if (claims.aud !== WORKER_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE) throw credentialError('worker_credential_invalid');
    const registered = requireRegisteredPrincipal(registry, claims.sub);
    verifyTimingSafeDomainSignature(
      decoded.payloadBytes, decoded.suppliedSignature,
      deriveSubjectGenerationKey(options.rootSecret, registered, WORKER_CREDENTIAL_DOMAIN),
    );
    assertCredentialClaimsEqualRegistry(claims, registered);
    if (claims.operationCatalogHash !== WORKER_MANAGEMENT_OPERATION_CATALOG_HASH) {
      throw credentialError('worker_credential_catalog_mismatch');
    }
    assertCanonicalPositiveBoundedTtl(claims.issuedAt, claims.expiresAt, MAX_TTL_MS, now);
    if (!claims.scopes.includes(expected.requiredScope)) throw credentialError('worker_credential_scope_denied');
    return deepFreeze(authenticatedPrincipalFromClaims(claims));
  }

  return Object.freeze({ issue, verify });
}

module.exports = Object.freeze({
  createWorkerCredentialAuthority, WORKER_CREDENTIAL_AUDIENCE, WORKER_CREDENTIAL_DOMAIN,
});
```

`shared/worker-management-catalog.cjs` is the executable CommonJS source of truth for the credential issuer, service, router, TypeScript/CJS clients, dashboard bridge, CLI registry, and public-contract generator. Rows are data only; all derived maps and the SHA-256 use these exact canonical rows. Every Worker path segment is `:worker`, including hard-stop, maintenance, settlement, and cutover operations that older hand-written clients mounted globally.

`src/workers/credential-authorities.ts` parses a tracked `home23.worker-credential-authorities.v1` document with `additionalProperties: false`. Each entry has exactly `id`, `kind`, fixed Keychain `service`/`account`, `secretSchema`, closed `consumers`, closed exact `hosts`, closed exact `operations`, `provisioning`, `rotation`, and `recoveryRegistry`; every array is nonempty, sorted/unique after canonicalization, rejects wildcards, and is part of the authority-definition hash. No secret value is legal in YAML, CLI argv, environment output, receipt, or model-visible data. The one common `resolveCredentialAuthorityUse()` accepts only a canonical authority ID plus a server-selected consumer/host/operation and validated profile binding; it re-resolves and validates ID, kind, schema, service, account, consumer, host, operation, record generation, persistent-reference identity, validation-profile membership/hash, and current profile generation before returning an opaque nonserializable use handle. It never returns raw secret bytes or a serializable `{ secret }` object, and it never falls back from an unknown/shorthand ID or unavailable least-privilege record to a broader authority. `worker credentials inventory <worker>`, `show`, and `validate` are read-only. `prepare` writes one content-addressed redacted `home23.worker-credential-change-plan.v1` beneath the supplied mode-`0700` approval root, binding worker, exact sorted authority ID set, current public record versions/fingerprints or missing status, proposed versions, reason, authority-definition hash, provisioning methods, expiry, nonce, and zero secret bytes. A conditional billing-identity rotation additionally requires `conditionReceipt` and binds the exact failed authorization hash, terminalization receipt hash, closed/replay-denied receipt hash, identity disposition `consumed_or_uncertain`, evidence hash, and record/version set; `proved_unconsumed`, an active/unclosed authorization, or changed condition bytes is rejected. `show --current-awaiting-approval` re-resolves that durable plan after a pause. Local `approve` displays and prompts for its exact canonical hash, authenticates the console operator with `home23-operator-primary`, and writes a signed single-use content-addressed approval receipt. `provision` and `rotate` require that exact plan hash/receipt, reject a different ID/version/reason/condition or consumed/expired approval, and use hidden prompts, generated cryptographic bytes, a permission-checked existing private authority, or an owned-browser OAuth flow according to each entry's fixed method. They write Keychain only after schema validation, consume the approval atomically with the intended record set, immediately read back persistent-reference identity and a domain-separated HMAC fingerprint, and emit a redacted hash-only receipt. Importing an existing site/Stripe/Supabase secret reads the named existing mode-`0600` authority directly into Keychain without printing it. The Gmail entry requests only `gmail.readonly`, validates the intended mailbox account and OAuth client/refresh authority, and rejects broader scopes. The owned-email entry is a versioned closed record containing the exact fresh address plus a generated strong signup password; both are non-serializable outside the fixed public-signup/browser adapter, survive browser/process restart under the same record version, and have operator recovery access through the Keychain record. A failed signup that consumed or may have consumed the address/password is never reset in place: provisioning rotates the complete record to a new version and any new canary requires a new hard-stop authorization/fingerprint. This task also owns the closed parser/handler registration for all `worker credentials` verbs and for local `worker schema-hard-stop approve|status`; Task 16 supplies the exact request/application workflow and tests. No later task may rely on a CLI verb first introduced in its live command block.

Tests require this exact 20-ID/service/account/kind/schema/consumer/provisioning/rotation set, the exact four closed validation-profile partitions above, role separation, `additionalProperties: false`, no value-like fields, no alias pointing at a different service, no wildcard host/operation, and no consumer capable of reading a record outside its declared deterministic adapter. Each profile is a disjoint required/deferred partition of the same 20 IDs; an unknown/ambiguous profile or `--require-all` is rejected. The eight new authorities are partitioned as seven `shakedown-observation-readonly` entries plus one `shakedown-indexing-write` fixed non-secret descriptor. The resolver checks capability consumer, schema, service, account, host, operation, generation, and profile partition; absent or drifted least privilege returns `unavailable_least_privilege` and never falls back to `site-runtime-production`, `stripe-live-runtime`, `supabase-cli-production`, service role, arbitrary SQL, or a model-visible value. The live inventory may truthfully report missing records; no task treats the tracked definition as proof that a secret exists.

The payment-settlement read surface is closed and cross-source. The one loopback payment-settlement operation is a typed aggregate read owned by `jerry-api`; for the exact authorization/window it returns only the existing webhook-ledger, profile, entitlement, and pending-subscription projections needed by the verifier. The two existing Supabase operations remain security-invoker, RLS-preserving read-only views filtered by the obligation-bound observer principal and provide an independent pending-subscription/funnel cross-check; this plan creates no parallel settlement views. The Stripe key is restricted to the ten listed object-read operations and cannot create, update, cancel, refund, detach, or delete anything. The durable authorization-replay decision comes directly from the owner-scoped Home23 store through `assertHardStopReplayDenied({ ownerAgent, authorizationHash })`, not through a site credential. Together these authorities cover Checkout Session, Subscription, Invoice, PaymentIntent, Charge, Refund, balance transaction, upcoming-invoice, PaymentMethod-attachment, webhook-ledger, profile, entitlement, and authorization-replay readback. Each route has a closed path/query/response schema in the Task 6 network authority, rejects list scans or an ID not already bound to the obligation, and returns only IDs/statuses, bounded amounts/timestamps, and HMAC-redacted linkage in receipts.

- [ ] **Step 4: Derive trigger and owner server-side**

`src/workers/auth.ts` resolves the authenticated principal from the exact subject registry, removes only documented legacy identity fields, rejects every other unknown public field, and resolves owner, trigger, scopes, and `authenticatedSourceRef` from trusted registries. Every owner-scoped non-operator principal must match the manifest owner. An operator crosses owners only with `worker:operator-cross-owner`; the obligation-bound settlement observer additionally matches the exact persisted obligation. Mount these routes before the global large-body parser with a small deterministic JSON ceiling. Missing/corrupt authority returns `503`; missing/malformed/invalid/expired credential returns `401`; scope/owner denial returns `403`; malformed/unknown body fields return `400`; absent authorized resources return `404`. Every denial occurs before handler/store access and no legacy unsecured router is mounted.

```ts
export async function authenticateWorkerPrincipal(
  request: express.Request,
  requiredScope: WorkerOperationScope,
  dependencies: WorkerAuthDependencies,
): Promise<AuthenticatedWorkerRequest> {
  if (!dependencies.credentialAuthority.available) throw new WorkerAuthError(503, 'credential authority unavailable');
  const token = readBearerToken(request.headers.authorization);
  const principal = dependencies.credentialAuthority.verify(token, { requiredScope });
  const worker = dependencies.registry.loadWorker(String(request.params.worker));
  if (principal.ownerAgent !== undefined && principal.ownerAgent !== worker.ownerAgent) {
    const crossOwner = principal.kind === 'operator' &&
      principal.scopes.includes('worker:operator-cross-owner');
    if (!crossOwner) throw new WorkerAuthError(403, 'principal owner mismatch');
  }
  return {
    principal,
    ownerAgent: worker.ownerAgent,
    trigger: principal.trigger,
    body: parsePublicWorkerBodyAfterRemovingKnownIdentityFields(request.body),
  };
}
```

After authentication, route handlers do not spread `req.body` into a trusted envelope. Add one builder and one closed source-resolution seam. The only public run fields are `mission`, `missionPath`, `expectedConsequence`, `requestedNarrowings`, `selectedHardStopAuthorizationHash`, and `collaborationHandoff`; the parser removes the documented legacy identity fields before rejecting every other field. In particular, public callers cannot provide `requestId`, idempotency, occurrence/event/job/pursuit/correlation/causation/origin identifiers, requester/source identity, active-grant identity, authorization binding, canonical input hash, or envelope hash.

```ts
declare const trustedRequestSourceBrand: unique symbol;

export type TrustedRequestSourceKind =
  | 'interactive' | 'scheduler-occurrence' | 'verified-event'
  | 'agency-next-action' | 'operator' | 'recovery';

export interface ResolvedTrustedRequestSource {
  readonly [trustedRequestSourceBrand]: true;
  readonly kind: TrustedRequestSourceKind;
  readonly sourceId: string;
  readonly canonicalSourceHash: string;
  readonly idempotencyKey: string;
  readonly occurrenceKey?: string;
  readonly pursuitId?: string;
  readonly jobId?: string;
  readonly eventId?: string;
  readonly originWorker?: string;
  readonly originRunId?: string;
  readonly originActionId?: string;
  readonly correlationId?: string;
  readonly causationId?: string;
}

export interface TrustedWorkerRequestProvenance {
  readonly schema: 'home23.worker-request-provenance.v1';
  readonly requester: string;
  readonly authenticatedSourceRef: string;
  readonly credentialId: string;
  readonly credentialGeneration: number;
  readonly operationCatalogHash: string;
  readonly sourceKind: TrustedRequestSourceKind;
  readonly sourceId: string;
  readonly canonicalSourceHash: string;
  readonly canonicalPublicInputHash: string;
  readonly originWorker?: string;
  readonly originRunId?: string;
  readonly originActionId?: string;
}

export interface TrustedWorkerRequestBuilderInput {
  readonly worker: string;
  readonly principal: AuthenticatedWorkerRequest['principal'];
  readonly publicInput: PublicWorkerRunInputV2;
  readonly source: ResolvedTrustedRequestSource;
}

export class TrustedWorkerRequestBuilder {
  constructor(private readonly dependencies: {
    registry: WorkerRegistry;
    hardStops: ActivatedHardStopBindingResolver;
  }) {}

  build(input: TrustedWorkerRequestBuilderInput): Readonly<TrustedWorkerRunEnvelope> {
    assertExactPublicRunInput(input.publicInput);
    assertBrandedTrustedSource(input.source);
    const worker = this.dependencies.registry.requireWorker(input.worker);
    assertPrincipalMayAddressOwner(input.principal, worker.ownerAgent);
    const canonicalPublicInputHash = sha256Canonical(input.publicInput);
    const stablePrincipal = stableRegisteredPrincipalProjection(input.principal);
    const requestIdentity = {
      schema: 'home23.worker-request-identity.v1' as const,
      ownerAgent: worker.ownerAgent,
      worker: worker.name,
      principalSubject: stablePrincipal.subject,
      credentialId: stablePrincipal.credentialId,
      authenticatedSourceRef: stablePrincipal.authenticatedSourceRef,
      idempotencyKey: input.source.idempotencyKey,
      canonicalSourceHash: input.source.canonicalSourceHash,
    };
    const requestId = deterministicWorkerRequestId(sha256Canonical(requestIdentity));
    const expectedConsequence = resolveRequiredExpectedConsequence({
      sourceKind: input.source.kind,
      mission: input.publicInput.mission,
      supplied: input.publicInput.expectedConsequence,
    });
    const hardStopAuthorization = input.publicInput.selectedHardStopAuthorizationHash
      ? this.dependencies.hardStops.resolveExactActiveBinding({
          selector: input.publicInput.selectedHardStopAuthorizationHash,
          worker: worker.name,
          principal: input.principal,
        })
      : undefined;
    const provenance: TrustedWorkerRequestProvenance = {
      schema: 'home23.worker-request-provenance.v1',
      requester: input.principal.subject,
      authenticatedSourceRef: input.principal.authenticatedSourceRef,
      credentialId: input.principal.credentialId,
      credentialGeneration: input.principal.generation,
      operationCatalogHash: workerManagementCatalogHash,
      sourceKind: input.source.kind,
      sourceId: input.source.sourceId,
      canonicalSourceHash: input.source.canonicalSourceHash,
      canonicalPublicInputHash,
      ...(input.source.originWorker ? { originWorker: input.source.originWorker } : {}),
      ...(input.source.originRunId ? { originRunId: input.source.originRunId } : {}),
      ...(input.source.originActionId ? { originActionId: input.source.originActionId } : {}),
    };
    return deepFreeze({
      requestId,
      worker: worker.name,
      ownerAgent: worker.ownerAgent,
      principal: stablePrincipal,
      trigger: input.principal.trigger,
      mission: input.publicInput.mission,
      missionPath: input.publicInput.missionPath,
      expectedConsequence,
      idempotencyKey: input.source.idempotencyKey,
      occurrenceKey: input.source.occurrenceKey,
      pursuitId: input.source.pursuitId,
      jobId: input.source.jobId,
      eventId: input.source.eventId,
      correlationId: input.source.correlationId ?? requestId,
      causationId: input.source.causationId,
      requestedNarrowings: input.publicInput.requestedNarrowings,
      hardStopAuthorization,
      provenance,
    });
  }
}
```

Only server-side resolvers may construct the branded source: the interactive resolver derives a fresh source/idempotency/correlation identity; Task 11 resolves a persisted scheduler occurrence; Task 12 resolves an immutable verified trigger plus durable causal ancestry; Task 13 resolves a persisted Agency next action; recovery reuses the original source bytes. The builder validates `canonicalSourceHash`, ensures correlation/causation ownership, and deep-freezes the result. `stableRegisteredPrincipalProjection()` keeps only registry-bound subject/kind/owner/scopes/trigger/credential ID and generation/catalog/source-reference fields; bearer bytes, signature, `issuedAt`, and `expiresAt` never enter a canonical request. `deterministicWorkerRequestId()` is a domain-separated canonical hash encoding of the shown identity tuple and does not include credential generation or token timing, so a retry with a freshly issued token for the same registered subject/source derives the same ID. Task 5 compares the canonical idempotency intent after excluding request ID and first-admission credential generation; it requires every other stable principal/source/public-input/authorization byte to match, returns the original stored envelope on a valid duplicate, and retains the first admission generation as separate immutable audit evidence. Credential rotation never rewrites that evidence, while a changed subject, credential ID, source reference/hash, public input, or authorization conflicts. `resolveRequiredExpectedConsequence()` accepts a nonempty bounded supplied consequence, supplies the exact registered interactive default `A verified Worker receipt states what changed, what was learned, or why no safe change was made.`, and rejects a missing consequence for every non-interactive source. Add `provenance`, `expectedConsequence`, and the three origin identifiers to the internal `TrustedWorkerRunEnvelope` in `src/workers/types.ts`; Task 5 hashes and stores that exact object. The selected hard-stop hash remains only an untrusted selector and is never copied; the resolver returns the verified `TrustedHardStopBinding` or rejects.

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement exact non-standing hard-stop document verification**

Verify the Ed25519 signature and canonical hash; exact principal, capability, Supabase project, Stripe/site account aliases, owned-identity alias, allowed operation set, cleanup-safety set, maximum amount and maximum net cost in minor units, currency, validity window, nonce, orchestration-plan/state-machine/runner/catalog/root-module/leaf-router/mailbox-adapter/operation-vocabulary/route-lock/cleanup-safety/redaction hashes, and `singleUse: true`. Require every main operation to come from `BILLING_CANARY_OPERATIONS`; require every safety operation to come from `BILLING_CANARY_CLEANUP_OPERATIONS`, with exact main overlap `cancel/refund/cleanup` and safety-only `expire-session`; and require the ordered main sequence to be valid under the shared billing transition table. Reject generic spend, wildcard targets/operations, absent cleanup bounds, standing use, hash drift, and browser/body-supplied operator identity. This task produces a verified immutable value only; Task 5 owns transactional activation/reservation/consumption after the store exists.

```ts
export async function verifyHardStopAuthorization(
  input: unknown,
  publicKeys: WorkerPublicKeyRegistry,
  expected: HardStopVerificationBindings,
  now = new Date(),
): Promise<Readonly<VerifiedHardStopAuthorization>> {
  const document = parseHardStopAuthorization(structuredClone(input));
  if (document.singleUse !== true) throw new Error('hard-stop authorization must be single-use');
  if (document.capabilityId !== 'shakedown.billing.production-canary') throw new Error('capability mismatch');
  if (document.accountTargets.length === 0 || document.accountTargets.some((target) => target.includes('*'))) {
    throw new Error('wildcard or empty account target');
  }
  assertExactBillingTargets(document, expected.billingTargets);
  assertExactPrivateIdentityAliases(document, expected.privateIdentityAliases);
  assertExactPrivateIdentityBindings(document, expected.privateIdentityBindings, expected.identityBindingHmacKey);
  assert.equal(document.privateIdentityBindingsHash, sha256Canonical(document.privateIdentityBindings));
  assert.equal(document.mailboxTargetHash, expected.mailboxTargetHash);
  assert.equal(document.mailboxAdapterDependencyClosureHash, expected.mailboxAdapterDependencyClosureHash);
  assert.equal(document.stripeApiVersion, expected.stripeApiVersion);
  assert.equal(document.stripeApiVersionAuthorityHash, expected.stripeApiVersionAuthorityHash);
  assert.equal(document.stripeApiVersionFreshnessReceiptHash,
    expected.stripeApiVersionFreshnessReceiptHash);
  assertFreshStripeApiVersionReceipt(expected.stripeApiVersionFreshnessReceipt, {
    stableAuthorityHash: document.stripeApiVersionAuthorityHash,
    explicitVersion: document.stripeApiVersion,
    maximumAgeSeconds: 86400,
  });
  assert.equal(document.productId, expected.productId);
  assert.equal(document.priceId, expected.priceId);
  assert.equal(document.maximumAmountMinor, expected.maximumAmountMinor);
  assert.equal(document.maximumNetCostMinor, expected.maximumNetCostMinor);
  assertSortedUniqueHttpsAuthorities(document.allowedCheckoutHosts);
  assertSortedUniqueHttpsUrls(document.checkoutCallbackUrls);
  assertSortedUniqueHttpsUrls(document.confirmationRedirectUrls);
  assert.equal(document.allowedCheckoutHostsHash, sha256Canonical(document.allowedCheckoutHosts));
  assert.equal(document.checkoutCallbackUrlsHash, sha256Canonical(document.checkoutCallbackUrls));
  assert.equal(document.confirmationRedirectUrlsHash, sha256Canonical(document.confirmationRedirectUrls));
  assertExactStringSet(document.allowedCheckoutHosts, expected.allowedCheckoutHosts);
  assertExactStringSet(document.checkoutCallbackUrls, expected.checkoutCallbackUrls);
  assertExactStringSet(document.confirmationRedirectUrls, expected.confirmationRedirectUrls);
  assert.equal(document.canaryCheckoutContractHash, expected.canaryCheckoutContractHash);
  assert.equal(document.canaryIdempotencyDerivationHash, expected.canaryIdempotencyDerivationHash);
  assert.equal(document.canarySessionJournalSchemaHash, expected.canarySessionJournalSchemaHash);
  assert.equal(document.cleanupSafetyPolicyHash, expected.cleanupSafetyPolicyHash);
  assert.equal(document.networkPolicyAuthorityHash, expected.networkPolicyAuthorityHash);
  assert.equal(document.networkBodySchemaHash, expected.networkBodySchemaHash);
  assertPinnedHardStopArtifacts(document, expected.immutableRunnerManifest);
  assertExactOperationVocabulary(document.allowedOperations, BILLING_CANARY_OPERATIONS);
  assertExactCleanupSafetyVocabulary(document.cleanupOperations, BILLING_CANARY_CLEANUP_OPERATIONS, {
    overlapWithMainAllowed: ['cancel', 'refund', 'cleanup'],
    safetyOnly: ['expire-session'],
  });
  assertValidBillingCanarySequence(document.allowedOperations);
  if (document.maximumAmountMinor < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(document.maximumAmountMinor)) {
    throw new Error('invalid maximum amount');
  }
  if (document.maximumNetCostMinor < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(document.maximumNetCostMinor)) {
    throw new Error('invalid maximum net cost');
  }
  assert.equal(document.maximumValiditySeconds, 14400);
  assert.equal(document.minimumExecutionWindowSeconds, 7200);
  assert.equal(document.cleanupReserveSeconds, 3600);
  if ((Date.parse(document.expiresAt) - Date.parse(document.notBefore)) / 1000 > document.maximumValiditySeconds) {
    throw new Error('authorization validity exceeds bound');
  }
  if (now < new Date(document.notBefore) || now >= new Date(document.expiresAt)) throw new Error('authorization expired or inactive');
  const publicRecord = await publicKeys.requireExactRole(
    document.signingKeyId, 'operator-authority', 'Ed25519',
  );
  const unsignedPayloadHash = sha256Canonical(withoutSignature(document));
  await publicRecord.verify(canonicalBytes(withoutSignature(document)), document.signature);
  const documentHash = sha256CanonicalSignedDocument(document);
  return deepFreeze({ document, unsignedPayloadHash, documentHash, standing: false });
}
```
