```js
export function buildPublicContract(routerManifest, eligibleDiscoveryManifest, concreteAssetManifest) {
  return Object.freeze({
  routes: routerManifest,
  caddyRoutes: ['/start', '/newsletter'],
  parameterizedRoutes: eligibleDiscoveryManifest.routes,
  api: ['/api/v1/shows', '/api/v1/search', '/api/v1/audio/:showId/:trackIndex',
    '/api/v1/user/favorites', '/api/v1/user/history'],
  assets: concreteAssetManifest.files.map((file) => Object.freeze({
    path: file.publicPath,
    sha256: file.sha256,
    contentType: file.contentType,
    minimumBytes: file.minimumBytes,
  })),
  assetFamilies: concreteAssetManifest.families,
  globals: ['ENV_CONFIG', 'trackPageView', 'trackShowView', 'trackEvent', 'trackEmailSignup',
    'trackUTMParameters', 'trackTwitterEvent', 'jerryPlayer', 'ensureJerryPlayer'],
  event: 'jerry:player',
  });
}

export async function verifySignedInPlayback(page, entitlementFixture) {
  if (!entitlementFixture?.owned || entitlementFixture.status !== 'active') {
    throw new Error('owned signed-in entitlement fixture required');
  }
  let historyWriteAttempted = false;
  await page.route('**/api/v1/user/history/**', async (route) => {
    if (route.request().method() === 'POST') {
      historyWriteAttempted = true;
      return route.fulfill({ status: 204, body: '' });
    }
    return route.continue();
  });
  await page.addInitScript(entitlementFixture.browserSessionScript);
  await page.goto(entitlementFixture.showUrl);
  const primaryPlay = page.getByRole('button', { name: /^(Play Show|Resume Show)$/ });
  await expect(primaryPlay).toHaveCount(1);
  await primaryPlay.click();
  await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.jerryPlayer?.currentTime)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  const showPause = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pause', exact: true });
  const showScrubber = page.getByRole('slider', { name: 'Scrub show playback', exact: true });
  await expect(showPause).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(showScrubber).toHaveCount(1);
  await showPause.click();
  await showScrubber.fill('15');
  await assertDurationRemainingAndNowPlaying(page);
  assert.equal(historyWriteAttempted, true);
  assert.equal(await authoritativeOwnedHistoryWriteCountDuringTest(), 0);
}
```

The concrete asset manifest never probes a directory root for `200`. In production, the candidate builder derives a signed exact-file manifest from the preserved/current live tree: mapped JSON, branding image, and icon used by the built document. The currently empty live `html/peaks` family is represented honestly by a hash-bound `asset_family_unavailable_empty_authority` receipt plus a proof that the candidate references zero `/peaks/*` URLs; it is not fabricated and does not block cutover. If a source-backed peak artifact later exists, the manifest must name and verify its exact file before any reference is emitted. Verification checks each available exact URL's status, content type, minimum bytes, and expected hash (or manifest-bound candidate hash) and separately checks audio `206`/`Content-Range`; `/peaks/`, `/branding/`, `/icons/`, or an SPA fallback can never satisfy the contract.

The verifier has an explicit `/subscribe` state matrix. In predeploy tests, tracker-failure signup uses only an ephemeral mocked Auth provider. In production before Task 32, it uses an already-owned session and checks route rendering, field semantics, client/server validation, and navigation without submitting; it asserts zero Auth/profile/checkout writes. The only real signup/checkout submission is Task 32's separately authorized canary. Candidate, post-cutover, and rollback verifier rows all carry the applicable matrix state and authoritative write counters. Signed-in playback acceptance similarly intercepts the additive `/user/history/:showId` POST at the browser boundary while allowing real public audio delivery, proves the request would be formed, and verifies the authoritative owned history count is unchanged. If a real history-row consequence is ever required, it needs its own explicitly bounded owned-data authorization; it is not smuggled into a read-only smoke.

The same verifier must compile and enforce the exact Task 20 `browser-api-security.v1.json` hash. Against the candidate/mock backend and, later, production it fetches every representative public and sensitive route, API/session/error response, OPTIONS preflight, Auth/payment callback, and audio range response; compares the complete CSP/security/cache headers; rejects credentialed reflection for disallowed origins; exercises an allowed same-origin cookie flow and an Origin-less native Bearer flow; verifies body/content-type ceilings and redacted Hono errors without sending secrets; proves Caddy's client-IP overwrite/trusted-peer contract; checks exact redirect allowlists; and captures a browser service-worker/module/script/connect/frame graph whose third-party origins equal the versioned inventory. - [ ] **Step 5: Cut over with an explicit journal and verifier reserve**

Journal `prepared -> snapshotted -> built -> tested -> cutover -> verifying -> committed`, fsyncing every state. Only the dedicated publisher can write the live tree. Reserve finite non-model budget for verifier and rollback. A failed or uncertain verifier immediately enters rollback; no model decision is needed.

```js
const SITE_RELEASE_TRANSITIONS = Object.freeze({
  prepared: 'snapshotted',
  snapshotted: 'built',
  built: 'tested',
  tested: 'cutover',
  cutover: 'verifying',
  verifying: 'committed',
});

export async function advanceSiteRelease(journal, expected, next, evidence) {
  if (SITE_RELEASE_TRANSITIONS[expected] !== next) throw new Error(`Invalid site release transition: ${expected} -> ${next}`);
  await journal.compareAndAppend({ expected, next, evidenceSha256: sha256(canonicalJson(evidence)) });
  await journal.fsync();
}

export async function finishVerification(context) {
  const verification = await withDeadline(context.verifier(), context.verifierBudgetMs);
  if (verification.status !== 'passed') return context.rollback.restorePredecessor(verification);
  return advanceSiteRelease(context.journal, 'verifying', 'committed', verification);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement verified object import plus patch-identity-aware code integration**

Accept only a tested commit at an exact dedicated ref in the independent worker clone. Export that ref as a run-scoped Git bundle, bind its SHA-256 into the normalized action and receipt, verify the bundle, and fetch it into a unique temporary `refs/codex-import/*` namespace in the operator repository. Only then prove the imported tip, expected baseline, ancestry, and patch identities; re-run the operator-checkout invariant; atomically create/update one configured `refs/heads/codex/shakedown-worker/*` ref; delete the temporary ref; and recheck the invariant. A missing prior canonical ref uses Git's zero object ID for compare-and-swap. No branch switch, worktree edit, index change, merge into the user's branch, hardlink/object sharing, or remote push is allowed.

```js
const ZERO_OID = '0'.repeat(40);

export async function integrateTestedCommit({
  repository, cloneRepository, candidateRef, candidateCommit, expectedBase,
  expectedPatchIds, canonicalRef, actionId, bundlePath,
}) {
  if (!canonicalRef.startsWith('refs/heads/codex/shakedown-worker/')) throw new Error('invalid canonical ref');
  if (!candidateRef.startsWith('refs/heads/codex/shakedown-worker/')) throw new Error('invalid candidate ref');
  await assertRefEquals(cloneRepository, candidateRef, candidateCommit);
  const importRef = `refs/codex-import/${actionId}`;
  await createGitBundle(cloneRepository, bundlePath, candidateRef);
  let canonicalUpdated = false;
  let previous: string | null = null;
  try {
    const bundleSha256 = await sha256File(bundlePath);
    await bindActionInputBeforeImport({ actionId, candidateCommit, candidateRef, bundleSha256 });
    await git(repository, ['bundle', 'verify', bundlePath]);
    const before = await captureOperatorCheckoutInvariant('/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com');
    previous = await resolveRefOrNull(repository, canonicalRef);
    await assertRefAbsent(repository, importRef);
    await git(repository, ['fetch', '--no-tags', bundlePath, `${candidateRef}:${importRef}`]);
    await assertRefEquals(repository, importRef, candidateCommit);
    await assertAncestor(repository, expectedBase, candidateCommit);
    await assertPatchIdentities(repository, candidateCommit, expectedPatchIds);
    await git(repository, ['update-ref', canonicalRef, candidateCommit, previous ?? ZERO_OID]);
    canonicalUpdated = true;
    const after = await captureOperatorCheckoutInvariant('/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com');
    if (canonicalJson(after) !== canonicalJson(before)) {
      throw new Error('operator checkout invariant changed');
    }
    return {
      canonicalRef, previous, current: candidateCommit, bundleSha256,
      operatorInvariantSha256: sha256(canonicalJson(after)),
    };
  } catch (error) {
    if (canonicalUpdated) {
      if (previous) await git(repository, ['update-ref', canonicalRef, previous, candidateCommit]);
      else await git(repository, ['update-ref', '-d', canonicalRef, candidateCommit]);
    }
    throw error;
  } finally {
    await deleteRefIfExact(repository, importRef, candidateCommit);
    await removeRunScopedBundle(bundlePath);
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement immutable backend release journals**

Materialize versioned source/builds beneath `releases/code`, record predecessor, dependency lock, build/test receipts, config fingerprint, and target PM2 process. Before prepare and again in the cutover transaction, query Task 5 through the authenticated management client and require the exact active deployment-maintenance fence subject/generation/receipt plus zero outstanding payment-settlement deployment block. Site, backend, stable-data, promoter, watchdog, and Caddy helpers accept a branded `VerifiedMaintenanceFenceLease`, not a caller boolean; they refuse direct execution without it. Journal `prepared -> snapshotted -> built -> tested -> cutover -> restarted -> verifying -> committed`; every uncertain post-restart state enters readback and then rollback or reconciliation.

```js
const BACKEND_RELEASE_TRANSITIONS = Object.freeze({
  prepared: 'snapshotted', snapshotted: 'built', built: 'tested', tested: 'cutover',
  cutover: 'restarted', restarted: 'verifying', verifying: 'committed',
});

export async function materializeBackendRelease(input) {
  const releaseParent = '/Users/jtr/websites/shakedownshuffle.com/releases/code';
  const buildInputs = {
    sourceCommit: input.sourceCommit,
    bunVersion: input.pinnedBunVersion,
    platform: input.pinnedPlatform,
    dependencyLockSha256: await hashBlobAtCommit(input.repository, input.sourceCommit, 'jerry-api/bun.lock'),
    buildCommandSha256: sha256Canonical(['bun', 'run', 'build']),
  };
  const releaseIdentity = sha256Canonical(buildInputs);
  const releaseRoot = join(releaseParent, `${input.sourceCommit}-${releaseIdentity.slice(0, 16)}`);
  if (await pathExists(releaseRoot)) {
    return verifyAndReuseExactBackendRelease(releaseRoot, input);
  }
  const stage = await mkdtemp(join(releaseParent, `.prepare-backend-${releaseIdentity}.`));
  const journal = await input.journal.prepareAndFsync({
    stage, releaseRoot, sourceCommit: input.sourceCommit, releaseIdentity, buildInputs,
  });
  try {
    await exportCommit(input.repository, input.sourceCommit, stage);
    await runFixed(['bun', 'install', '--frozen-lockfile', '--production'], {
      cwd: join(stage, 'jerry-api'), env: minimalDependencyInstallEnvironment(),
    });
    await runFixed(['bun', 'run', 'build'], {
      cwd: join(stage, 'jerry-api'), env: isolatedReleaseEnvironment({ NODE_PATH: '' }),
    });
    const dependencyClosureSha256 = await hashProductionDependencyClosure(join(stage, 'jerry-api'));
    await smokeRelocatedJerryApi(join(stage, 'jerry-api'), {
      hideExternalNodeModules: true, forbidAncestorResolution: true, minimalEnvironment: true,
    });
    const manifest = {
      schema: 'home23.shakedown-backend-release.v1',
      sourceCommit: input.sourceCommit,
      releaseIdentity,
      buildInputs,
      predecessor: input.predecessor,
      dependencyLockSha256: await sha256File(join(stage, 'jerry-api/bun.lock')),
      dependencyClosureSha256,
      processName: 'jerry-api',
      payloadTreeSha256: await sha256TreeExcluding(stage, ['release-manifest.json']),
    };
    await writeJsonAtomicFsync(join(stage, 'release-manifest.json'), manifest, 0o600);
    const manifestSha256 = await sha256File(join(stage, 'release-manifest.json'));
    await fsyncTreeAndDirectory(stage);
    await chmodTreeReadOnly(stage);
    await rename(stage, releaseRoot);
    await fsyncDirectory(releaseParent);
    return { ...manifest, manifestSha256, status: 'created', releaseRoot };
  } catch (error) {
    await quarantineJournalOwnedStage(stage, journal, error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

`payloadTreeSha256` deliberately excludes `release-manifest.json`; the separately signed/hashed manifest binds that payload hash, avoiding an impossible self-referential tree digest. Code-release addressing includes the exact commit, lock, pinned Bun/platform, and fixed build-command identity, so a toolchain change cannot collide at a commit-only path. Runtime configuration is deliberately absent from the immutable code identity. `verifyAndReuseExactBackendRelease()` recomputes the build-input identity, excluded-manifest payload hash, and manifest hash, then checks commit, lock, production dependency closure, modes, signature, and relocated minimal-environment boot; it never overwrites a mismatch. Failpoints cover export, dependency install, build, smoke, manifest, chmod, and pre/post rename. A journal-owned partial stage may be quarantined, but an existing final path is immutable and is either byte-identically reused or rejected.

At deployment, `backend-runtime-identity.mjs` creates a separate signed `BackendRuntimeIdentity` over code release manifest/hash plus environment-authority hash, exact non-secret config hash, secret-name/value-hash authority, stable-data pointer/hash, PM2 definition hash, process name, and exact listener set `127.0.0.1:3005` public plus `127.0.0.1:3006` internal canary. Rotation of any runtime binding produces a new deployment identity and journal even when code bytes are reused; it never tries to rematerialize or overwrite the code release.

The code release contains only a config-independent PM2 definition compiler/launcher whose bytes are part of the payload tree; it does not contain a generated environment-specific ecosystem file or environment-authority hash. At deployment, `backend-runtime-identity.mjs` materializes the single-process `jerry-api` definition beneath the restricted stable root `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/shakedown-runtime-data/runtime/backend-deployments/<backendRuntimeIdentity>/jerry-api.ecosystem.cjs`. That signed mode-`0600` definition pins the absolute immutable built entrypoint, release `cwd`, exact Bun interpreter, fixed args, `SHAKEDOWN_DATA_ROOT`, active-backend pointer, and restricted environment-authority hash. A config rotation therefore creates a new runtime-identity directory/definition while byte-identically reusing the code release. It never copies `.env` into the release. Inventory all currently required non-secret variables and secret variable names from the predecessor, place secret values only behind fixed Keychain aliases or a mode-`0600` restricted environment snapshot outside Git/releases/model context, and make the hash-pinned launcher resolve them at process start. Missing/wrong variable, alias, hash, interpreter, cwd, or entrypoint fails before PM2 reload.

Before cutover, journal the exact predecessor `pm_exec_path`, `pm_cwd`, interpreter, args, filtered environment-value hashes, process ID/state, and a restricted reconstructable predecessor ecosystem definition. Reload only `jerry-api` from the candidate ecosystem with update-env semantics; `pm2 jlist` plus the process-reported release commit/config/data-root must equal the candidate manifest. Rollback reloads the recorded predecessor definition—not a plain restart—and verifies its exact readback. All PM2 effects and rollback transitions share the backend journal and recovery lock; failpoints cover before/after definition reload, process start, readback, and pointer update.

```js
export async function switchBackendDefinition(context, backendRuntimeIdentity) {
  const identity = await readAndVerifyBackendRuntimeIdentity(backendRuntimeIdentity, {
    codeReleaseRoot: context.immutableCodeReleaseRoot,
    restrictedDeploymentRoot: context.restrictedRoot,
    environmentAuthority: context.environmentAuthority,
    stableDataAuthority: context.stableDataAuthority,
  });
  const candidate = await readRestrictedRuntimePm2Definition(identity.pm2DefinitionPath);
  await assertDefinitionBindsBackendRuntimeIdentity(candidate, identity);
  const predecessor = await context.pm2.captureExactDefinition('jerry-api', context.restrictedRoot);
  await context.journal.appendAndFsync('backend_definition_prepared', { candidate, predecessor });
  await context.pm2.startOrReloadExact(candidate, { only: 'jerry-api', updateEnv: true });
  const readback = await context.pm2.readExact('jerry-api');
  await assertBackendRuntimeIdentity(readback, identity, {
    requireCodeReleaseManifestHash: true,
    requireEnvironmentConfigDataPointerHashes: true,
  });
  await context.journal.appendAndFsync('backend_definition_verified',
    hashOnly({ candidate, predecessor, readback, backendRuntimeIdentity: identity.sha256 }));
  return { candidate, predecessor, readback, backendRuntimeIdentity: identity.sha256 };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Reuse the watchdog recovery owner and one shared lock**

Add the missing shared recovery lock to `ops/shakedown-watchdog/lib/watchdog-core.mjs`; make both worker and launchd wrapper acquire it before any `jerry-api` start/restart. Replace the wrapper's hard-coded dirty-checkout script with the immutable active-backend-release pointer and validate its manifest before start. Worker runtime capabilities may invoke only `jerry-api`, the retained `com.jtr.caddy-static` owner for fixed `shakedown-audio-static` recovery, and the fixed Caddy action below. Audio recovery acquires its dedicated lock, retains the current runtime strategy, and verifies a catalog-pinned byte-range canary at port `18089`; it never treats a root `404` as failure or changes the service owner. Dynamic DNS and runtime-strategy changes are denied.

```js
export const RUNTIME_TARGETS = Object.freeze({
  'jerry-api': {
    owner: 'com.jtr.shakedown-watchdog',
    lock: 'shakedown-jerry-api-recovery',
    processName: 'jerry-api',
    healthUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3005/health',
  },
  'shakedown-audio-static': {
    owner: 'gui/501/com.jtr.caddy-static',
    lock: 'shakedown-audio-static-recovery',
    processName: 'com.jtr.caddy-static',
    port: 18089,
    probeMethod: 'GET',
    probeHeaders: { Range: 'bytes=0-1023' },
    acceptedStatuses: [200, 206],
  },
});

export async function withRecoveryLock(lockName, action) {
  const lock = await acquireFencedRecoveryLock({
    path: `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/shakedown-runtime-data/locks/${lockName}.lock`,
    mode: 0o600,
    heartbeatIntervalMs: 10_000,
    recoveryGraceMs: 45_000,
    processIdentity: await readMacProcessIdentity(process.pid),
    // identity is boot-session + PID + immutable process-start token + executable hash.
    // A timestamp alone can never authorize stealing.
  });
  try { return await action(); } finally { await lock.release(); }
}
```

`acquireFencedRecoveryLock()` creates the no-follow lock with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, writes and fsyncs `{ schema, bootSessionId, pid, processStartToken, executableSha256, nonce, device, inode, fencingGeneration, heartbeatSequence, heartbeatAt }`, keeps the original descriptor open, and heartbeats through that descriptor while the action runs. Contention first checks the path's device/inode and record signature, then proves the exact PID/start-token/executable tuple. A live exact owner is never stolen even if its heartbeat is old or paused by a slow restart. Reclaim is allowed only when the heartbeat exceeds the recovery grace **and** macOS process readback proves the exact owner tuple is dead or the boot session differs; indeterminate readback fails closed. Reclaim compare-checks device/inode/nonce immediately before unlink, acquires with a monotonically persisted fencing generation, and fsyncs the lock directory. Caddy overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` with `{remote_host}` for the Jerry API proxy and strips `Forwarded`; internal port `3006` never appears. Any failure restores exact predecessor bytes, validates/reloads them, and verifies restoration. Thus Caddyfile is never a general write root, and the path cannot touch `gui/501/com.jtr.caddy-static`.

For the backend, the same deployment identity requires the exact Task 20 policy/config hash, browser-session/audio-ticket schema hashes, `NODE_ENV=production`, both loopback listeners, and the stable runtime key/value-hash authority. Boot fails if the browser-session wrap/CSRF/audio-ticket key fields are absent from `site-runtime-production`, if the public listener is not loopback, or if error/debug policy is widened. The audio-static path can only reacquire the `shakedown-audio-static-recovery` lock, invoke the retained `gui/501/com.jtr.caddy-static` owner, and verify the pinned byte-range canary; it cannot switch the audio runtime strategy, process label, port, root, or Caddy route.

```js
export const SCOPED_RELOAD_SERVICES = Object.freeze(new Set([
  'caddy', 'jerry-api', 'shakedown-audio-static',
]));

export async function reloadCaddy(context, operation) {
  const configPath = '/Users/jtr/server/config/Caddyfile';
  if (!new Set(['validate-reload-exact', 'apply-browser-api-security-policy']).has(operation.kind)) {
    throw new Error('unknown typed Caddy operation');
  }
  const predecessor = await context.snapshot.captureCaddy(configPath, 'system/homebrew.mxcl.caddy');
  const selected = operation.kind === 'validate-reload-exact'
    ? await context.caddy.verifyExactUnchanged(configPath, predecessor.sha256)
    : await context.caddy.compileTypedSecurityCandidate({
      configPath,
      predecessorSha256: predecessor.sha256,
      policyPath: 'ops/shakedown-worker/config/browser-api-security.v1.json',
      expectedPolicySha256: operation.securityPolicySha256,
      allowedBlocks: ['shakedown-bare', 'shakedown-www', 'shakedown-api'],
      forbidUpstreamRootHostOrUnrelatedDirectiveChange: true,
    });
  await context.command.runFixed(['caddy', 'validate', '--config', selected.candidatePath]);
  await context.caddy.publishExactCandidateAndFsync(selected, configPath);
  await context.command.runFixed(['caddy', 'reload', '--config', configPath]);
  const routes = await context.verify.routes([
    'https://shakedownshuffle.com/', 'https://www.shakedownshuffle.com/',
    'https://www.shakedownshuffle.com/api/v1/shows?limit=1',
    'https://api.shakedownshuffle.com/health',
    'https://api.shakedownshuffle.com/api/v1/shows?limit=1',
    'https://www.shakedownshuffle.com/start',
    'https://www.shakedownshuffle.com/newsletter',
    context.pinnedArticleUrl,
    'https://www.shakedownshuffle.com/pro/',
    context.pinnedPublicAudioCanaryUrl,
  ]);
  const security = await context.verify.browserApiSecurity({
    policySha256: operation.securityPolicySha256,
    requireExactHeadersCspAndCors: true,
    requireLivePreflightAndScriptGraph: true,
    requireNoPublicUpstream3006: true,
    requireNativeBearerCompatibility: true,
  });
  if (routes.status !== 'passed' || security.status !== 'passed') {
    await context.snapshot.restoreValidateReloadAndReadBackCaddy(predecessor);
    return { status: 'restored', configPath, routes, security };
  }
  return { configPath, owner: 'system/homebrew.mxcl.caddy', routes, security,
    policyHash: operation.securityPolicySha256 };
}

export async function recoverAudioStatic(context, pinnedCanaryPath) {
  assertPinnedCatalogAudioPath(pinnedCanaryPath);
  return withRecoveryLock('shakedown-audio-static-recovery', async () => {
    const label = 'gui/501/com.jtr.caddy-static';
    const before = await context.launchd.captureExactState(label, {
      includeProcessGeneration: true, includeRootPortRouteConfigHashes: true,
    });
    await context.journal.appendAndFsync('audio_recovery_predecessor', hashOnly(before));
    try {
      await context.launchd.kickstartExact(['launchctl', 'kickstart', '-k', label]);
      const readback = await context.http.get(`http://127.0.0.1:18089${pinnedCanaryPath}`, {
        headers: { Range: 'bytes=0-1023' },
      });
      const after = await context.launchd.captureExactState(label, {
        includeProcessGeneration: true, includeRootPortRouteConfigHashes: true,
      });
      if (readback.status !== 206 || !readback.headers['content-range']) throw new Error('audio range canary failed');
      if (after.processGeneration === before.processGeneration) throw new Error('audio owner did not restart');
      assert.deepEqual(after.invariantHashes, before.invariantHashes);
      await context.journal.appendAndFsync('audio_recovery_verified', hashOnly({ after, readback }));
      return { owner: label, lock: 'shakedown-audio-static-recovery', port: 18089,
        before, after, kickstartArguments: ['-k', label], readback };
    } catch (error) {
      const rollback = await context.launchd.restoreExactEnabledStateAndRecoverSameLabel(label, before);
      await context.journal.appendAndFsync('audio_recovery_restored', hashOnly(rollback));
      return { status: 'restored_predecessor_state', rollback };
    }
  });
}
```

`prepareStableDataAuthority()` is non-live preparation only and never writes an already-live stable root from a retired legacy snapshot. `finalizeStableDataCutover()` is allowed only inside Task 31's global deployment epoch after both exact legacy ingresses read back `PAUSED`, all replacement schedules read back disabled/fenced, no legacy or replacement consequential run is in flight, and the billing/backend/site maintenance fence is held. It acquires backend, collection, enrichment, non-audio, release-promotion, legacy-writer, and billing locks; rereads and hashes the current legacy authority exactly once for an `initial-cutover`; reconciles it into a new same-filesystem stable snapshot; compares schema/counts/protected fields; and journals one atomic pointer set for backend plus every active writer/promoter. The backend is then started on that stable root while the old frontend remains live, and old-frontend/new-backend compatibility is proved before any frontend switch or schedule activation. A legitimate fresh source hash is migration input, not unexplained drift.

For `already-applied-same-epoch` and `already-applied-upgrade`, the stable data pointer is authoritative: verify its manifest, journal schema/modes, active writers, and protected hashes and never recapture retired checkout-relative data or roll the pointer backward. An upgrade fences the current replacement schedules, retains legacy `PAUSED`, and uses the previous replacement epoch as its rollback target. If a failure occurs before stable-data commit, restore the fully journaled legacy/data/backend predecessor as one unit. After stable-data commit, recovery may roll the data pointer back only when the same epoch owns a tested lossless pointer journal that reconciles every intervening write/event; absent that proof, it keeps stable data live and rolls code/schedules to the prior replacement epoch or leaves both consequence ingresses paused. It never re-enables a legacy writer against the new authority.

```js
export async function finalizeStableDataCutover(context) {
  const quiescence = await context.cutover.verifyIngressFence({
    receipt: context.automationCutoverReceipt,
    requireLegacyPaused: true,
    requireReplacementDisabledOrFenced: true,
    requireNoInFlightLegacyRun: true,
    requireNoInFlightReplacementRun: true,
    requireNoDualConsequentialIngressWindow: true,
  });
  return context.locks.withAllOrdered(EXACT_SHAKEDOWN_WRITER_LOCKS, async (fence) => {
    const source = context.epoch.mode === 'initial-cutover'
      ? await context.legacyAuthority.captureFresh()
      : await context.stableAuthority.verifyExistingManifestAndWriters();
    const snapshot = context.epoch.mode === 'initial-cutover'
      ? await context.stableAuthority.reconcileFreshSnapshot(source)
      : await context.stableAuthority.readCurrentSnapshot();
    await context.verifier.assertSchemaCountsProtectedFields(source, snapshot);
    const journal = await context.cutover.prepareAndFsync({ source, snapshot, fence });
    const switched = await context.pointers.compareAndSwapAll({
      expected: journal.predecessorPointers,
      replacement: journal.stablePointers,
    });
    const readback = await context.verifier.apiAndPublic(switched);
    if (readback.status !== 'verified') return context.cutover.rollbackAll(journal, readback);
    return context.cutover.commit(journal, { readback, ingressFenceReceipt: quiescence });
  });
}
```

After the initial pointer set is live, every collection or enrichment pointer mutation uses `stable-data-pointer.mjs`. The canonical pointer is a no-follow mode-`0600` document containing schema, generation, tree/config/manifest hashes, predecessor generation/hash, committed lane/action/journal IDs, and committed-at time. Both lanes retain separate candidate/snapshot/journal/receipt types, but acquire one common ordered lock `stable-data:pointer-mutation` before their lane lock (`stable-data:collection` or `stable-data:enrichment`), re-read the current pointer under the lock, and compare-and-swap only from the exact expected generation and bytes. Commit fsyncs the lane result tree and journal before an atomic no-replace pointer temporary/rename/parent fsync, then reads back generation/hash and records it in the lane journal. A stale candidate must revalidate/rebase from the newer authority; it cannot overwrite it.

Rollback is equally conditional: it may restore its predecessor only while the current pointer still equals the exact generation/tree/lane-result produced by that journal. If another lane has advanced the pointer, rollback writes `reconciliation_required`, preserves the newer pointer, and leaves its own candidate/snapshot for review. Startup scans both lane journals under the common lock and resolves a crash to either the exact predecessor or exact committed lane result from pointer bytes/generation; it never guesses by mtime. Tests interleave collection/enrichment prepare, commit, readback, failure, rollback, and crash at every fsync/rename boundary, prove monotonic generation, no deadlock/dual current pointer/lost update, and ensure one lane's rollback cannot erase the other's later result.

```js
export async function mutateStableDataPointer({ lane, expectedPointer, candidate, journal }, deps) {
  return deps.locks.withAllOrdered([
    'stable-data:pointer-mutation', `stable-data:${lane}`,
  ], async (fence) => {
    const current = await deps.pointer.readNoFollowAndVerify();
    assertExactPointerGenerationAndBytes(current, expectedPointer);
    const prepared = await journal.prepareCandidateAndFsync({ current, candidate, fence });
    await deps.verifier.verifyCandidate(prepared);
    const replacement = Object.freeze({
      ...prepared.pointerFields,
      generation: current.generation + 1,
      predecessorGeneration: current.generation,
      predecessorSha256: current.sha256,
      lane,
      journalId: journal.id,
    });
    await deps.pointer.compareAndSwapFsync({ expected: current, replacement });
    const readback = await deps.pointer.readNoFollowAndVerify();
    assertExactPointerGenerationAndBytes(readback, replacement);
    await journal.commitAndFsync({ replacement: readback });
    return readback;
  });
}

export async function rollbackStableDataPointer(laneResult, deps) {
  return deps.locks.withAllOrdered([
    'stable-data:pointer-mutation', `stable-data:${laneResult.lane}`,
  ], async () => {
    const current = await deps.pointer.readNoFollowAndVerify();
    if (!pointerEqualsLaneResult(current, laneResult)) {
      return deps.journal.reconciliationRequired('current pointer advanced by another lane');
    }
    return deps.pointer.compareAndSwapFsync({ expected: current, replacement: laneResult.predecessor });
  });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the wrapper around existing authority and lock seams**

Read the current collection authority receipt before action. Re-parse the strict config, verify its profile/grant-pinned hash, resolve every stable-data/audio/quarantine/candidate/stash target, and prove required volumes are present. Acquire the existing daily orchestration/shared promotion lock. Invoke only fixed repository commands with `./config.json`, capture each native receipt, and synthesize one parent capability receipt without hiding child semantic state.

```js
export function createCollectionCapability({ authority, config, lock, commands, receipts }) {
  return {
    async runDaily(input) {
      const current = await authority.read();
      const resolved = await config.verifyPinnedTargets(input.profile, input.grant);
      return lock.withLock('jerry-collection:daily', async () => {
        const children = [];
        for (const name of ['non-audio:daily:local', 'non-audio:verify', 'collection:daily:local']) {
          const child = await commands.runNpmScript(name, ['--config', './config.json'], resolved);
          children.push(child);
          if (child.semanticStatus === 'waiting_for_batch_pair') break;
          if (!['completed', 'no_change'].includes(child.semanticStatus)) throw new Error(`collection child failed: ${name}`);
        }
        return receipts.commitParent({ capability: 'shakedown.collection.local', authority: current, children });
      });
    },
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Add promotion preflight and consequence proof**

Before promotion, validate candidate schema, hashes, source provenance, non-regression counts, overwrite set, public/API compatibility, stable data-authority hash/generation, and rollback snapshot. In this task, exercise promotion only against a copied fixture authority/API/public root. The real additive promotion and readback occur in Task 31 after activation. The collection lane keeps its own release journal but delegates the final pointer commit and any rollback to Task 22's common ordered `stable-data:pointer-mutation` coordinator. Verify the fixture authority, API route, and page; otherwise request conditional rollback. Rollback is allowed only while current pointer generation/hash still equals this collection result; if enrichment or another collection action advanced it, preserve current truth, quarantine this candidate, and return `reconciliation_required`.

```js
export async function promoteCollectionCandidate(input, deps) {
  const checked = await deps.preflight.verify({
    capability: 'shakedown.collection.promote-additive',
    candidate: input.candidate,
    expectedDataRootHash: input.profile.dataRootHash,
    expectedConfigHash: input.profile.collectionConfigHash,
    requireNoOverwrite: true,
  });
  const snapshot = await deps.promoter.snapshot(checked.target);
  try {
    const promoted = await deps.pointerCoordinator.mutate({
      lane: 'collection', expectedPointer: checked.expectedPointer,
      candidate: await deps.promoter.prepareAdditive(checked), journal: deps.collectionJournal,
    });
    const readback = await deps.verifier.verifyApiAndPublic(promoted);
    if (readback.status !== 'verified') throw new Error('collection readback failed');
    return deps.receipts.commit({ status: 'completed', snapshot, promoted, readback });
  } catch (error) {
    await deps.pointerCoordinator.rollbackIfCurrentEqualsLaneResult({
      lane: 'collection', snapshot, promoted: deps.collectionJournal.lastPromotedResult(),
    });
    await deps.quarantine.write({ candidateHash: checked.candidateHash, reason: String(error) });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Wrap the existing enrichment pipeline as typed prepare, validate, promote, verify, and rollback operations**

Carry canonical show identity, source family, citations, normalization decisions, curator status, old/new hashes, protected-field diff, and candidate schema through every stage. No generated narrative may overwrite audio identity, date, venue, track, or source metadata.

```js
const PROTECTED_SHOW_FIELDS = Object.freeze(['id', 'date', 'venue', 'tracks', 'audioSources']);

export function createEnrichmentCapability({ authority, planner, runner, verifier, receipts }) {
  const capability = 'shakedown.enrichment';
  return {
    async prepare(input) {
      const source = await authority.verifySourcePolicy(input.sourceBundle);
      if (!source.accepted) return receipts.quarantined(source);
      const candidate = await planner.build({ ...input, source, protectedFields: PROTECTED_SHOW_FIELDS });
      return receipts.prepared(candidate);
    },
    async promote(input) {
      if (input.receiptType !== 'shakedown.enrichment.candidate.v1') throw new TypeError('enrichment receipt required');
      const result = await runner.promote(input);
      const readback = await verifier.verifyApiAndPublic(result);
      return readback.status === 'verified'
        ? receipts.completed({ capability, result, readback })
        : runner.rollback({ capability, result });
    },
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Make promotion independent from collection**

Use a separate release journal, lane lock, snapshots, verifier, receipt type, and automation replacement proof. Only the final pointer mutation lock/generation CAS is common with collection and is always acquired before the enrichment lane lock. A collection success cannot mark enrichment complete, and enrichment failure cannot freeze the collection lane. Enrichment rollback delegates to the common coordinator and proceeds only if current pointer bytes/generation exactly equal its own result; otherwise it records `reconciliation_required` without touching the newer collection authority.

```js
export const ENRICHMENT_LANE = Object.freeze({
  orderedLocks: ['stable-data:pointer-mutation', 'stable-data:enrichment'],
  lock: 'stable-data:enrichment',
  journal: 'shakedown.enrichment.release.v1',
  candidate: 'shakedown.enrichment.candidate.v1',
  consequence: 'shakedown.enrichment.consequence.v1',
});

export function assertEnrichmentLane(receipt) {
  if (receipt.schema !== ENRICHMENT_LANE.candidate) throw new TypeError('enrichment receipt required');
  return receipt;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Turn opportunities into evidence-bound content packages**

Require opportunity identity, audience need, cited source bundle, canonical target, claim inventory, UTM campaign, intended consequence, channel fit, expiry/freshness, and correction plan. Generate owned-site, Substack, and channel variants from one factual package while respecting each channel's format. Reject unsupported claims, repetitive thin content, and output created only to satisfy a cadence.

```js
export function prepareContentPackage({ opportunity, sources, campaign, renderers, now }) {
  if (opportunity.status !== 'selected' || !opportunity.evidenceHashes?.length) throw new Error('supported opportunity required');
  if (sources.some((source) => !opportunity.evidenceHashes.includes(source.sha256))) throw new Error('uncited source');
  if (Date.parse(opportunity.expiresAt) <= now.getTime()) throw new Error('stale opportunity');
  const base = Object.freeze({
    opportunityId: opportunity.id,
    canonicalUrl: opportunity.canonicalUrl,
    claims: opportunity.claims,
    sourceHashes: sources.map((source) => source.sha256),
    utmCampaign: campaign.utmCampaign,
    intendedConsequence: campaign.intendedConsequence,
    correctionPlan: campaign.correctionPlan,
  });
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(renderers).map(([channel, render]) => [channel, render(base)]));
}
```

All three delivery lanes use `delivery-effect.mjs` and Task 9's canonical destination outbox; adapter-local maps are caches only. The fixed runner context exposes a non-model-visible `deliveryEffects` bridge bound to the current `AuthorizedAdapterInvocation`. `reserve()` transactionally inserts one logical effect/outbox row keyed by `{ actionId, destinationClass, accountTargetHash, contentHash, recipientSetHash }`. Immediately before provider dispatch, while holding the exact destination lock, the adapter refreshes account identity plus (for communications) consent, suppression, unsubscribe, bounce, quiet-hour, cooldown, and rate-limit state; `start()` atomically stores those evidence hashes and a deterministic provider marker/idempotency key and fsyncs `started` before any provider/browser call. An expired freshness watermark denies and requires another readback; it never widens authority.

Every configured adapter must declare one tested exact reconciliation strategy. Substack embeds deterministic action/content marker metadata in the single draft/publication and searches the authoritative account's drafts/publications by that marker and canonical URL. A non-Substack provider uses its native idempotency/metadata key and GET readback. A consented send uses a deterministic provider idempotency key plus RFC Message-ID/campaign marker and an authoritative sent-message/provider API lookup by the opaque recipient-set hash. If a provider cannot prove zero or one effect, that account cannot be enabled. On resume from `started` without terminal, the adapter always reconciles first: exactly one matching provider object commits the existing effect; more than one or non-authoritative/ambiguous state becomes `reconciliation_required`; zero remains in reconciliation until the catalog-pinned consistency/crossing window proves absence, after which only the same idempotency key/marker may dispatch. It never creates a new key/action to escape uncertainty.

```js
export async function deliverExactlyOnce(input, context, adapter) {
  const effect = await context.deliveryEffects.reserve({
    actionId: context.actionId,
    destinationClass: input.destinationClass,
    accountTargetHash: input.accountTargetHash,
    contentHash: input.contentHash,
    recipientSetHash: input.recipientSetHash ?? sha256Canonical([]),
  });
  if (effect.status === 'terminal') return effect.terminalReceipt;
  if (effect.status === 'started') return reconcileStartedDelivery(effect, context, adapter);
  const fresh = await context.deliveryEffects.readFreshDispatchEligibility(effect, {
    requireAccountIdentity: true,
    requireConsentAndSuppression: input.destinationClass === 'consented-communications',
    maximumAgeMs: input.eligibilityMaximumAgeMs,
  });
  if (fresh.decision !== 'allow') return context.deliveryEffects.deny(effect, fresh);
  const marker = deriveDeterministicProviderMarker(effect.logicalEffectId, input.contentHash);
  const started = await context.deliveryEffects.startAndFsync(effect, { marker, freshEvidenceHash: fresh.sha256 });
  const existing = await adapter.authoritativeReadbackByMarker(started.marker);
  if (existing.cardinality === 1) return context.deliveryEffects.commitTerminal(started, existing);
  if (existing.cardinality !== 0 || existing.crossingProof !== 'provider_authoritative_complete') {
    return context.deliveryEffects.reconciliationRequired(started, existing);
  }
  const accepted = await adapter.dispatch({ ...input, marker: started.marker,
    idempotencyKey: started.providerIdempotencyKey });
  const readback = await adapter.authoritativeReadbackByMarker(started.marker, accepted);
  if (readback.cardinality !== 1) return context.deliveryEffects.reconciliationRequired(started, readback);
  return context.deliveryEffects.commitTerminal(started, readback);
}
```

Failpoints cover after reservation, after fresh-consent readback, after `started` fsync, after provider acceptance before local commit, after provider readback, and before/after terminal/outbox acknowledgement. Process restart at each point proves one durable effect row, at most one provider consequence, replay denial, and preservation of uncertainty rather than blind repeat.

- [ ] **Step 4: Reconcile and wrap deterministic Substack adapters**

Choose local, Chrome, or Safari only from configured current capability/readiness receipts. Preflight authenticated account identity and destination, create or update exactly one idempotent draft/publication, perform authoritative URL/account readback, and record correction/unpublish capability. Browser navigation that creates state is classified as a write and stays behind the standing grant.

```js
export function createSubstackAdapter({ readiness, local, chrome, safari }) {
  const adapters = Object.freeze({ local, chrome, safari });
  return {
    async publish(input, context) {
      const current = await readiness.resolve(input.accountAlias);
      const adapter = adapters[current.adapter];
      if (!adapter || current.accountHash !== input.expectedAccountHash) throw new Error('Substack preflight mismatch');
      return deliverExactlyOnce({ ...input, destinationClass: 'substack' }, context, {
        dispatch: (request) => adapter.publishOneMarkedDraftOrPublication(request),
        authoritativeReadbackByMarker: (marker, accepted) =>
          adapter.readbackExactAccountMarkerAndCanonicalUrl(marker, input.canonicalUrl, accepted),
      });
    },
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement at least one real non-Substack public adapter**

Resolve the first enabled `public-non-substack` registry entry to a typed module with fixed account, host, content class, rate limit, cooldown, URL rules, preflight, publish, authoritative readback, and correction. A missing or unauthenticated configured account is a lane-local failure, not permission to substitute an arbitrary platform.

```js
export function resolvePublicChannel(registry, adapters) {
  const entry = registry.channels.find((channel) => channel.kind === 'public-non-substack' && channel.enabled);
  if (!entry) return { status: 'unavailable', lane: 'public-non-substack' };
  const adapter = adapters[entry.adapterId];
  if (!adapter) throw new Error(`unregistered channel adapter: ${entry.adapterId}`);
  return Object.freeze({
    entry,
    preflight: (input) => adapter.preflight({ ...input, host: entry.host, accountAlias: entry.accountAlias }),
    publish: (input, context) => deliverExactlyOnce({
      ...input, destinationClass: 'public-non-substack',
      accountTargetHash: entry.accountTargetHash,
      rateLimit: entry.rateLimit, cooldown: entry.cooldown,
    }, context, {
      dispatch: (request) => adapter.publish({ ...request, host: entry.host, accountAlias: entry.accountAlias }),
      authoritativeReadbackByMarker: (marker, accepted) =>
        adapter.readbackByExactProviderMarker({ marker, accepted, host: entry.host,
          accountAlias: entry.accountAlias }),
    }),
    readback: adapter.readback.bind(adapter),
    correct: adapter.correct.bind(adapter),
  });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Implement consented one-to-one communications safely**

Consume only the existing eligible-candidate contract with documented consent basis. Use opaque recipient IDs until the provider boundary; enforce suppression, unsubscribe, bounce, prior-contact, quiet hours, per-recipient and global rate limits, cooldown, content hash idempotency, and a correction/escalation procedure. No bulk-send or purchased/scraped-contact path exists.

```js
export async function sendConsentedCommunication(candidate, context, deps) {
  assertOpaqueRecipientOnly(candidate);
  return deliverExactlyOnce({
    ...candidate,
    destinationClass: 'consented-communications',
    recipientSetHash: sha256Canonical([candidate.opaqueRecipientId]),
    accountTargetHash: candidate.accountTargetHash,
    eligibilityMaximumAgeMs: 5_000,
  }, context, {
    async dispatch(request) {
      // deliveryEffects.startAndFsync() has already persisted the immediately-fresh
      // consent/suppression/rate-limit hash and deterministic provider marker.
      const resolved = await deps.recipientBoundary.resolveNonSerializable(candidate.opaqueRecipientId);
      return deps.provider.sendOne({
        recipientHandle: resolved,
        content: candidate.content,
        providerIdempotencyKey: request.idempotencyKey,
        messageId: deterministicMessageId(request.marker),
        campaignMarker: request.marker,
      });
    },
    authoritativeReadbackByMarker: (marker, accepted) =>
      deps.provider.readSentMessageByExactMarkerAndOpaqueRecipientHash({
        marker, accepted, recipientSetHash: sha256Canonical([candidate.opaqueRecipientId]),
      }),
  });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Reconcile current pipeline promotion gates**

Preserve readiness and `automationPromotionPlan.applyAllowed` as distinct facts. A green scan alone never authorizes unattended application. Replace free-form browser/manual steps with typed state transitions and native child receipts.

```js
export function decidePipelineTransition({ readiness, automationPromotionPlan, authority }) {
  if (readiness.status !== 'green') return { status: 'blocked_readiness' };
  if (automationPromotionPlan.applyAllowed !== true) return { status: 'prepared_not_authorized' };
  if (authority.decision !== 'allow') return { status: authority.decision };
  return {
    status: 'dispatch_typed_action',
    capability: authority.channelKind === 'substack'
      ? 'shakedown.distribute.substack'
      : 'shakedown.distribute.channel',
    operation: 'publish',
    evidenceHashes: [readiness.sha256, automationPromotionPlan.sha256, authority.grantHash],
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add deterministic social-image validation and bounded repair**

Validate canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter tags, image fetch, MIME, dimensions, byte size, content hash, alt text, and cache visibility. Generate or select a source-relevant image only through the configured asset path; publish it through the site release capability into the Task 21 staged fixture and verify crawler-visible staged output. Never silently reuse a broken or unrelated image. Task 31 performs the required real repair/validation consequence after standing-grant activation.

```js
export async function verifyOrRepairSocialImage(artifact, deps) {
  const metadata = await deps.metadata.read(artifact.canonicalUrl);
  const image = await deps.fetchImage(metadata.ogImage);
  const valid = metadata.twitterImage === metadata.ogImage && image.mime.startsWith('image/') &&
    image.width >= 1200 && image.height >= 630 && image.bytes <= deps.maxBytes && metadata.alt?.trim();
  if (valid) return { status: 'verified', imageHash: image.sha256 };
  const selected = await deps.assets.selectSourceRelevant({ sourceHashes: artifact.sourceHashes, canonicalUrl: artifact.canonicalUrl });
  const candidate = await deps.siteRelease.stageSocialImage({ artifact, selected });
  const readback = await deps.metadata.read(candidate.stagedUrl);
  if (readback.ogImageHash !== candidate.imageHash) throw new Error('staged social image readback failed');
  return { status: 'repair_candidate', candidate };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Schedule timed one-shot readbacks from action receipts**

Every publication/distribution receipt creates configured short, medium, and mature readback due events using the scheduler occurrence contract. Readbacks join the campaign's immutable UTM/canonical identity to Matomo behavior and authoritative aggregate conversion state. Missing evidence remains missing; it is not scored as zero unless route/watermark/filter/crossing proof supports zero.

```js
export function campaignReadbackOccurrences(receipt, windows) {
  return ['short', 'medium', 'mature'].map((windowName) => ({
    kind: 'workerRun',
    worker: 'shakedown-jerry',
    mission: 'campaign-readback',
    dueAt: new Date(Date.parse(receipt.committedAt) + windows[windowName]).toISOString(),
    idempotencyKey: `${receipt.campaignId}:${receipt.actionId}:${windowName}`,
    input: { campaignId: receipt.campaignId, utm: receipt.utm, canonicalUrl: receipt.canonicalUrl, windowName },
  }));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Update channel and content scores transparently**

Use reach quality, listening depth, return behavior, signup/entitlement conversion, correction/failure cost, and confidence. Apply sample-size floors and uncertainty. Store the old score, evidence, rule version, new score, and next decision. Retire, revise, or cool down weak recurring work; do not optimize for posting volume.

```js
export function scoreMatureCampaign({ priorScore, evidence, ruleVersion, minimumSample }) {
  if (evidence.sampleSize < minimumSample || evidence.maturity !== 'mature') return { status: 'readback_pending' };
  const quality = 0.2 * evidence.reachQuality + 0.2 * evidence.listeningDepth +
    0.15 * evidence.returnRate + 0.3 * evidence.verifiedConversionRate -
    0.15 * evidence.correctionFailureCost;
  const confidence = Math.min(1, evidence.sampleSize / (minimumSample * 4));
  const newScore = priorScore * (1 - confidence) + quality * confidence;
  return {
    status: 'scored', priorScore, newScore, confidence, ruleVersion,
    decision: newScore < evidence.retirementFloor ? 'retire_or_change' : 'continue',
    evidenceHashes: evidence.hashes,
  };
}
```

```js
export function projectShakedownWorkerDesk(state) {
  const link = (row) => ({
    ...row,
    evidenceUrl: `/home23/api/workers/${encodeURIComponent(state.worker)}` +
      `/runs/${encodeURIComponent(row.runId)}/receipt#${encodeURIComponent(row.receiptId)}`,
  });
  const campaignsByLane = state.campaigns.map(link).reduce((groups, row) => {
    (groups[row.lane] ??= []).push(row);
    return groups;
  }, {});
  return Object.freeze({
    opportunities: state.opportunities.filter((row) => row.status === 'open').map(link),
    campaignsByLane,
    readbacks: state.readbacks.map(link),
    channelScores: state.channelScores.map(link),
    discovery: link(state.discovery), socialImages: link(state.socialImages), funnel: link(state.funnel),
    conversionAuthority: link(state.conversionAuthority), collection: link(state.collection),
    enrichment: link(state.enrichment), rollbacks: state.rollbacks.map(link), retired: state.retired.map(link),
  });
}
```

```ts
export async function inventoryLegacyMaterials(rootAliases: LegacyRootAlias[], restricted: RestrictedManifestWriter) {

  const runtimeRows = discovered.map((record) => ({
    rootAlias: record.rootAlias,
    relativeClass: requireSanitizedRelativeClass(record.relativeClass),

  await restricted.writeMode0600Manifest(runtimeRows);
  return runtimeRows.map(({ rootAlias, relativeClass, pathHmac, sourceHash, size, provenanceClass }) => ({
    rootAlias, relativeClass, pathHmac, sourceHash, size, provenanceClass,
  }));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Reconcile every imported item against current authority**

`src/workers/knowledge-import.ts` and its CLI classify each factual assertion as verified-current, durable principle, historical-only, superseded, conflicted, or unverified. Promote only durable ethos/process principles to the tracked playbook. Emit verified-current operational facts as provenance-bound state/memory-candidate events so canonical receipts/outboxes generate `MEMORY.md`; do not hand-edit that projection. Quarantine stale pricing, paths, metrics, publishing assumptions, runtime claims, credentials, direct contact identifiers, and account state.

```ts
export type KnowledgeStatus = 'verified-current' | 'durable-principle' | 'historical-only' |
  'superseded' | 'conflicted' | 'unverified';

export function classifyLegacyAssertion(assertion: LegacyAssertion, authority: CurrentAuthority): ClassifiedAssertion {
  const forbidden = assertion.tags.some((tag) => ['credential', 'direct-contact', 'account-state'].includes(tag));
  if (forbidden) return { ...assertion, status: 'unverified', destination: 'quarantine' };
  const match = authority.lookup(assertion.subject);
  if (assertion.kind === 'principle' && !match?.conflict) return { ...assertion, status: 'durable-principle', destination: 'playbook' };
  if (!match) return { ...assertion, status: 'unverified', destination: 'quarantine' };
  if (match.sha256 === assertion.valueHash) return { ...assertion, status: 'verified-current', destination: 'state-event' };
  return { ...assertion, status: match.supersedes(assertion) ? 'superseded' : 'conflicted', destination: 'quarantine' };
}
```

```ts
export function absorbAutomation(row: LegacyAutomationRow): AutomationDisposition {
  if (!row.definitionHash || !row.rollbackOperation) throw new Error(`incomplete automation row: ${row.id}`);
  return {
    id: row.id,
    deterministicExecutor: row.deterministicExecutor,
    targetCapability: requireKnownCapability(row.targetCapability),
    targetTrigger: requireKnownTrigger(row.targetTrigger),
    selectionRule: row.selectionRule,
    failureLessons: row.failureLessons,
    requiredEvidence: row.requiredEvidence,
    legacyJudgmentLoopEnabled: false,
    definitionHash: row.definitionHash,
    receiptRoots: row.receiptRoots,
    rollbackOperation: row.rollbackOperation,
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement strict proof orchestrators**

The generic verifier gathers build/test output, request/attempt journals, queue/lease recovery, scheduler/event exact-once behavior, existing-worker parity, concurrent-worker isolation, resource-lock behavior, Agency consequence attachment, outbox acknowledgements, cancellation, retry, revocation, and restart persistence. The Shakedown verifier consumes site-side receipts and the live-proof matrix. Both reject stale evidence, incomplete wrappers, missing bindings, synthetic live claims, unverified rollback, and status flattening.

```js
export async function verifyProofBundle(bundle, { now, maxAgeMs, requiredRows }) {
  const missing = requiredRows.filter((row) => !bundle.receipts[row]);
  const stale = Object.entries(bundle.receipts)
    .filter(([, receipt]) => now - Date.parse(receipt.committedAt) > maxAgeMs)
    .map(([row]) => row);
  const invalid = [];
  for (const [row, receipt] of Object.entries(bundle.receipts)) {
    const bound = ['commitHash', 'manifestHash', 'grantHash', 'requestId', 'runId', 'attemptId']
      .every((key) => typeof receipt[key] === 'string' && receipt[key].length > 0);
    if (!bound || receipt.wrapperStatus === 'interrupted' || receipt.rollback?.status === 'unverified' ||
        receipt.syntheticLiveClaim === true || receipt.flattenedStatus === true) invalid.push(row);
  }
  return { status: missing.length || stale.length || invalid.length ? 'failed' : 'passed', missing, stale, invalid };
}

const vb = (...names) => names.map((name) => [name, { arity: 0, repeatable: false }]);
const vv = (...names) => names.map((name) => [name, { arity: 1, repeatable: false }]);
const vr = (...names) => names.map((name) => [name, { arity: 1, repeatable: true }]);
const verifierMode = (effect, ...groups) => Object.freeze({
  effect,
  flags: Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(groups.flat())),
});

export const IMMUTABLE_RUNNER_MATERIALIZER_MODE_SPECS = Object.freeze({
  runner: verifierMode('materialize-immutable-runner',
    vv('--clone-root', '--source-commit', '--source-baseline', '--release-root', '--journal-root',
      '--signing-authority-id'),
    vb('--require-clean-tested-commit', '--require-lock-hashes', '--require-pinned-node-bun-npm-platform',
      '--require-fixed-build-command-identity', '--require-journal-owned-stage',
      '--require-keychain-signature', '--fsync-tree-and-parent', '--atomic-no-replace',
      '--reuse-only-byte-identical', '--print-release-path')),
});

export function parseClosedImmutableRunnerMaterializerInvocation(argv) {
  const parsed = parseModeAndFlags(argv);
  const spec = IMMUTABLE_RUNNER_MATERIALIZER_MODE_SPECS[parsed.mode];
  if (!spec) throw new TypeError(`unsupported immutable runner materializer mode: ${parsed.mode}`);
  validateExactFlagArityAndRepeatability(parsed.flags, spec.flags);
  validateRequiredAndAtLeastOneFlags(parsed.flags, {
    required: ['--clone-root', '--source-commit', '--source-baseline', '--release-root', '--journal-root',
      '--signing-authority-id', '--require-clean-tested-commit', '--require-lock-hashes',
      '--require-pinned-node-bun-npm-platform', '--require-fixed-build-command-identity',
      '--require-journal-owned-stage', '--require-keychain-signature', '--fsync-tree-and-parent',
      '--atomic-no-replace', '--reuse-only-byte-identical', '--print-release-path'],
  });
  if (parsed.signingAuthorityId !== 'operator-document-signing') {
    throw new TypeError('immutable runner requires operator-document-signing authority');
  }
  return Object.freeze(parsed);
}

export const ACTION_PLAN_VERIFIER_MODES = Object.freeze({
  generic: new Set(Object.entries(GENERIC_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS)
    .filter(([, spec]) => spec.effect === 'enqueue-action-plan').map(([mode]) => mode)),
  shakedown: new Set(Object.entries(SHAKEDOWN_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS)
    .filter(([, spec]) => spec.effect === 'enqueue-action-plan').map(([mode]) => mode)),
});
const HARD_STOP_ACTION_PLAN_MODES = new Set([
  'billing-production-lifecycle',
  'billing-cleanup-restart-continuity',
  'write-billing-failure-handoff',
]);

export function parseClosedVerifierInvocation(family, argv) {
  const registries = { generic: GENERIC_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS, shakedown: SHAKEDOWN_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS };
  const specs = registries[family];
  if (!specs) throw new TypeError(`unsupported verifier family: ${family}`);
  const parsed = parseModeAndFlags(argv);
  const spec = specs[parsed.mode];
  if (!spec) throw new TypeError(`unsupported verifier mode: ${parsed.mode}`);
  validateExactFlagArityAndRepeatability(parsed.flags, spec.flags);
  validateRequiredAndAtLeastOneFlags(parsed.flags, VERIFIER_MODE_CONSTRAINTS[family]?.[parsed.mode] ?? {});
  return Object.freeze({ ...parsed, effect: spec.effect });
}

export async function runVerifierMode(family, mode, parsed, deps) {
  const registries = { generic: GENERIC_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS, shakedown: SHAKEDOWN_VERIFIER_MODE_SPECS };
  const spec = registries[family]?.[mode];
  if (!spec) throw new TypeError(`unsupported verifier mode: ${mode}`);
  if (spec.effect === 'enqueue-action-plan') {
    const request = compileTypedWorkerActionPlan(family, mode, parsed, {
      worker: family === 'shakedown' ? 'shakedown-jerry' : parsed.worker,
      immutableRunnerManifest: await deps.deployedManifests.resolveVerifiedActiveRunner(family),
    });
    const accepted = HARD_STOP_ACTION_PLAN_MODES.has(mode)
      ? await deps.management.enqueueHardStopRun(request.worker, parsed.authorizationHash, request.publicPlan)
      : await deps.management.enqueueRun(request.worker, request.publicPlan);
    const terminal = await pollCanonicalTerminalReceipt({
      requestId: accepted.requestId,
      deadline: request.pollDeadline,
      getRequest: (requestId) => deps.management.getRequest(request.worker, requestId),
    });
    return verifyActionPlanReceiptBindings(mode, request, terminal);
  }
  if (spec.effect === 'proof-write') {
    const proof = await verifyReceiptBundleReadOnly(mode, parsed, deps.receipts);
    return deps.proofWriter.writeContentAddressedWithinCanonicalRoot(proof);
  }
  return verifyReceiptBundleReadOnly(mode, parsed, deps.receipts);
}
```

`compileTypedWorkerActionPlan()` returns a frozen `{ worker, publicPlan, pollDeadline, expectedBindings }`. For generic mode `deployed-forbidden-action-denial`, it accepts no caller-selected capability, operation, target, or arguments: it emits only fixed probe ID `repository-destructive-site-delete-v1`, which asks the deployed executor to evaluate the repository-denied destructive site-delete intent against the verified active runner. Success is only a canonical terminal receipt proving `decision='deny'`, zero adapter invocation, zero provider/filesystem effect, and the expected release/profile/policy hashes. The mode uses the existing authenticated `enqueueRun()` management client and adds no route. `pollDeadline` is derived from the selected closed verifier profile and immutable runner timeout ceiling, never from an undeclared CLI flag or caller body; polling expiry does not cancel, repeat, or reinterpret an in-flight consequential action and instead returns its request ID for later canonical readback.

The production script receives no site filesystem writer, browser controller, provider client, shell/process executor, PM2/Caddy/launchd adapter, Supabase/Stripe mutation client, or automation-product client. For an action-plan mode its only effectful dependency is the authenticated `WorkerManagementClient.enqueueRun()` method; all browser/provider/process effects occur later inside the already authorized immutable runner capability and are represented by its terminal receipts. Read-only modes consume deployed receipts/readbacks. Proof-write modes may atomically create or reuse only content-addressed artifacts beneath the canonical Home23 verification root. Dependency-injection tests make any direct effect call throw and scan imports for forbidden adapters.

`site-production-proof` unconditionally invokes the same closed `browser-api-security` verifier against the live release and production origin; its existing closed invocation therefore proves the exact deployed policy hash, headers/CSP/CORS graph, browser-cookie/CSRF/audio-ticket flow, native Bearer compatibility, server authorization, error redaction, redirect ceilings, trusted-proxy behavior, and production `NODE_ENV` without adding caller-selected policy flags. `paired-data-backend-frontend-cutover` likewise applies only Task 22's typed Caddy security-policy transition and requires the resulting live security readback before it can commit the site phase. Neither mode may downgrade the security matrix to a staged-only assertion.

Keep the broker/runtime construction in the existing `home23-jerry-harness` and `home23-forrest-harness`; no Worker process, port, socket server, Shakedown daemon, engine, brain, MCP, or scheduler is generated. First implement one mandatory code/state/config resolver in TypeScript and CommonJS. `HOME23_CODE_ROOT` is an exact read-only release beneath the sibling authority `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime/<commit>`; `HOME23_STATE_ROOT` is the existing stable `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23` state authority during this cutover; `HOME23_CONFIG_ROOT` is the immutable release's tracked public `<codeRoot>/config`; `HOME23_PRIVATE_CONFIG_ROOT` is the stable `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/config` authority but is readable only for an explicit ignored/private allowlist such as `secrets.yaml`, local device/cron state, and non-Git operator overrides; and `HOME23_WORKER_ROOT` remains `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers`. Thus the signed grant/channel/key/template bytes committed in Tasks 17/28/29 deploy with the immutable release instead of being read stale from dirty main, while private values never enter the release. The release parent is realpath-disjoint from state/private-config roots and from the dirty source worktree. Code imports/static dashboard assets/scripts and tracked public configuration resolve only beneath code root. Instances, workspaces, brains, conversations, logs, runs, runtime files, scheduler state, device registries, skill-sync output, worker SQLite/state, and projections resolve only through typed state paths. Private config resolution is closed by filename/schema and every public/private config hash is read back separately. Explicit external Shakedown/project roots remain separate configured authorities.

```ts
export interface Home23RuntimeRoots {
  codeRoot: string;
  stateRoot: string;
  configRoot: string;
  privateConfigRoot: string;
  workerRoot: string;
}

export function resolveHome23RuntimeRoots(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Readonly<Home23RuntimeRoots> {
  const roots = {
    codeRoot: requireAbsoluteRealDirectory(env.HOME23_CODE_ROOT),
    stateRoot: requireAbsoluteRealDirectory(env.HOME23_STATE_ROOT),
    configRoot: requireAbsoluteRealDirectory(env.HOME23_CONFIG_ROOT),
    privateConfigRoot: requireAbsoluteRealDirectory(env.HOME23_PRIVATE_CONFIG_ROOT),
    workerRoot: requireAbsoluteRealDirectory(env.HOME23_WORKER_ROOT),
  };
  assertPathWithin(roots.configRoot, roots.codeRoot);
  assertPathWithin(roots.privateConfigRoot, roots.stateRoot);
  assertPathWithin(roots.workerRoot, roots.stateRoot);
  assertDisjoint(roots.codeRoot, roots.stateRoot);
  return deepFreeze(roots);
}
```

Configuration secrets and `.env` values remain outside the release behind the private config authority/Keychain; the release manifest binds only names and value hashes.

The immutable `home23.worker-runtime-release.v1` manifest is content-addressed outside the code tree at `instances/workers/runtime/release-manifests/<manifest-sha256>.json`, mode `0400`. It declares `implementationCommit`, absolute `codeRoot`, `payloadTreeSha256`, `treeHashAlgorithm: home23.sorted-path-mode-content.v1`, `payloadFileCount`, `nodeExecutablePath`, `nodeExecutableSha256`, `restartScriptPath`, `restartScriptSha256`, `restartCommandArgv`, `restartCommandArgvCanonicalJson`, `restartCommandArgvSha256`, `restartCommandSha256`, `workerVerifierPath`, `workerVerifierSha256`, `shakedownVerifierPath`, `shakedownVerifierSha256`, `home23CliPath`, `home23CliSha256`, `guardedPm2SavePath`, `guardedPm2SaveSha256`, `keychainHelperPath`, `keychainHelperSha256`, and a closed `verifierProfiles` map whose entries each contain a fixed `family`, `argv`, `argvCanonicalJson`, and `argvSha256`. `restartScriptSha256` hashes only the script bytes. `restartCommandArgvSha256` hashes the exact UTF-8 `restartCommandArgvCanonicalJson` scalar, and `restartCommandSha256` hashes the domain-separated tuple of Node executable hash, restart-script hash, and argv hash; none is reused for another field. The manifest builder proves each canonical JSON scalar decodes to exactly its adjacent array, and that `restartCommandArgv` starts with `restartScriptPath`. Every declared command/helper/CLI path is nonempty, relative, segment-normalized, and resolves beneath the immutable `codeRoot`; every verifier profile is closed and test-enumerated. The deployment process spawns the resolved Node executable with the resolved script plus the selected manifest argv using `shell: false`; all post-deploy management and PM2-save commands execute only the resolved `home23CliPath`/`guardedPm2SavePath` with exact hashes; production CLI Keychain access spawns only the resolved immutable helper with its exact file hash and rejects `InMemoryKeychain` or a helper beneath mutable state/worktree paths. No caller command string, alternate path, extra flag, environment expansion, or mutable-worktree executable is accepted.

The active pointer has schema `home23.worker-runtime-active-pointer.v1` and contains `deploymentJournalId`, `deploymentJournalPath`, `releaseManifestPath`, `releaseManifestSha256`, `codeRoot`, `implementationCommit`, `payloadTreeSha256`, `home23CliSha256`, `guardedPm2SaveSha256`, `keychainHelperSha256`, and the predecessor pointer hash. Its referenced mode-`0600` deployment journal must have schema `home23.worker-runtime-deployment.v1`, the same `deploymentId`, terminal state `committed`, and exact `activePointerSha256`, `committedManifestSha256`, `committedCodeRoot`, `committedImplementationCommit`, `committedPayloadTreeSha256`, `committedHome23CliSha256`, `committedGuardedPm2SaveSha256`, `committedKeychainHelperSha256`, `verifierProfile`, `verifierPath`, `verifierSha256`, `verifierArgv`, `verifierArgvCanonicalJson`, and `verifierArgvSha256`. Use the following literal bootstrap contract at the start of every production command block in Tasks 30–33 and again after every pause/restart/maturity wait. It uses only fixed OS binaries and inline shell, never a resolver from the worktree or candidate release. The release builder rejects control characters/newlines in payload paths and defines `home23.sorted-path-mode-content.v1` as the sorted NUL-delimited sequence of type, mode, relative path, and file-content hash (or symlink target); the identical fixture-tested `home23_tree_hash` body below is copied verbatim into each production block. Successful resolution exports exactly `active_pointer`, `deployment_journal_id`, `deployment_journal`, `release_manifest`, `release_manifest_sha256`, `active_code_root`, `active_implementation_commit`, `active_payload_tree_sha256`, `node_executable`, `node_executable_sha256`, `worker_verifier`, `worker_verifier_sha256`, `shakedown_verifier`, `shakedown_verifier_sha256`, `home23_cli`, `home23_cli_sha256`, `guarded_pm2_save`, `guarded_pm2_save_sha256`, `worker_keychain_helper`, `worker_keychain_helper_sha256`, `restart_script`, `restart_script_sha256`, `restart_command_argv_json`, `restart_command_argv_sha256`, and `restart_command_sha256`.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

node_executable=$(/bin/realpath "$(json_raw "$release_manifest" nodeExecutablePath)")

test -x "$node_executable"
test "$(sha256_file "$node_executable")" = "$node_executable_sha256"
worker_verifier=$(require_safe_relative_file "$(json_raw "$release_manifest" workerVerifierPath)")

test "$(sha256_file "$worker_verifier")" = "$worker_verifier_sha256"
test "$journal_verifier_path" = "$worker_verifier"
test "$journal_verifier_sha256" = "$worker_verifier_sha256"
shakedown_verifier=$(require_safe_relative_file "$(json_raw "$release_manifest" shakedownVerifierPath)")

restart_script=$(require_safe_relative_file "$(json_raw "$release_manifest" restartScriptPath)")

test "$(sha256_file "$restart_script")" = "$restart_script_sha256"
restart_command_argv_json=$(json_raw "$release_manifest" restartCommandArgvCanonicalJson)
restart_command_argv_sha256=$(json_raw "$release_manifest" restartCommandArgvSha256)
test "$(/usr/bin/printf '%s' "$restart_command_argv_json" | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')" = "$restart_command_argv_sha256"
restart_command_sha256=$(json_raw "$release_manifest" restartCommandSha256)
test "$(/usr/bin/printf 'home23.command.v1\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' \
  "$node_executable_sha256" "$restart_script_sha256" "$restart_command_argv_sha256" | \
  /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')" = "$restart_command_sha256"
export active_pointer deployment_journal_id deployment_journal release_manifest \
  release_manifest_sha256 active_code_root active_implementation_commit active_payload_tree_sha256 \
  node_executable node_executable_sha256 worker_verifier worker_verifier_sha256 \
  shakedown_verifier shakedown_verifier_sha256 \
  home23_cli home23_cli_sha256 \
  guarded_pm2_save guarded_pm2_save_sha256 \
  worker_keychain_helper worker_keychain_helper_sha256 \
  restart_script restart_script_sha256 \
  restart_command_argv_json restart_command_argv_sha256 restart_command_sha256
```
