Any failed check is a fail-closed deployment/production-verification blocker. Tasks 31–33 may execute `"$node_executable" "$worker_verifier" ...` or `"$node_executable" "$shakedown_verifier" ...` only after that same block succeeds in the current shell. Restart execution is only through the deployment module's `spawn(node_executable, [restart_script, ...decodedFixedArgs], { shell: false })` after it proves the decoded fixed args equal both manifest argv encodings and the three command hashes; no shell evaluation of `restart_command_argv_json` is permitted.

`scripts/deploy-home23-worker-runtime.mjs` accepts one tested immutable release manifest, roots above, exact affected PM2 names, predecessor definitions, one closed manifest verifier-profile name, and the journal-defined rollback operation. It rejects caller-supplied command strings, argv, shell, verifier/restart paths, or environment-selected executables. It resolves the Node executable, verifier, fixed profile argv, and hashes only from the candidate manifest, then uses `spawn(..., { shell: false })`. It refuses a release missing the Task 1 preserved patch identities, both root and `engine/package-lock.json` dependency closures, distinct restart-file/argv/command hashes, verifier hashes/profiles, full payload-tree hash/non-writability, or root-classification proof. The release contains a generated release-specific ecosystem definition for exactly the six processes, with absolute entrypoint/cwd paths beneath the release and the exact stable root environment. Before the deployment journal, predecessor inspection is strictly read-only and returns canonical definition hashes/bytes in memory; it cannot materialize a snapshot. The mode-`0600` journal is then created and fsynced beneath `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/deployments`, after which it owns creation/fsync/readback of the restricted predecessor snapshot and records a `snapshotted` transition before any DB, pointer, PM2, or process effect. A crash before snapshot creation resumes only if fresh definitions still equal the journaled identity; a crash after snapshot fsync reuses exact bytes; mismatch/corruption freezes without an effect. Every later journal append/transition, DB transition, definition switch, pointer temporary-file write/rename and parent-directory sync, process transition, readback, and terminal state is durably fsynced before the next effect. `deploy --receipt-path-only` and journal-scoped `reconcile --receipt-path-only` return only a content-addressed mode-`0600` `home23.worker-runtime-deployment-result.v1` receipt. Its closed terminal state is `committed`, `rolled_back`, or `frozen`; it binds the deployment ID, manifest hash, journal path/hash, admission mode, active-pointer path/hash when committed, exact predecessor-restoration proof and a retry-required receipt when rolled back, or an urgent recovery receipt when frozen. Every result and nested restoration/retry/urgent proof lives beneath `/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/deployment-results`, is named by its SHA-256, and exposes the exact paired `*Path`/`*Sha256` fields consumed by Step 9. The CLI returns success to the shell only after the selected terminal proof is fsynced and read back; missing, nonterminal, mismatched, or unknown result fields fail closed.

Deployment admission is a closed two-way union. `first-deploy-bootstrap` exists only when the new Worker schema is absent, both owner harnesses report the Worker runtime disabled, there is no active pointer or prior deployment journal, and the Task 1 preservation inventory plus stable-root scan proves no Worker grant activation, cutover, billing authorization/settlement, or legacy Worker consequence authority can exist. That branch uses a content-addressed local bootstrap-admission receipt and the deployment lease/journal, not an impossible call to the not-yet-deployed management service; all live capabilities stay inactive through first boot. If bootstrap crashes after schema creation, only the same journal's elected recovery may resume or roll it back—schema presence can never authorize a fresh bootstrap. `managed-redeploy` covers every later deployment (including exact-same release repair and a changed candidate): before a deployment journal is created, the already active release must pass the protected pointer/journal/manifest resolver, an authenticated management call must acquire the exact `home23-runtime-deploy` maintenance fence bound to this deployment ID, and a fresh authoritative settlement readback must prove no payment/deployment block. The fence allows only that exact owning action/operation; site, backend, stable-data, payment, and sibling deployment operations are denied before their journals.

```js
export const WORKER_RUNTIME_PROCESSES = Object.freeze([
  'home23-jerry-harness', 'home23-forrest-harness',
  'home23-jerry', 'home23-forrest', 'home23-jerry-dash', 'home23-forrest-dash',
]);

export const DEPLOYMENT_STATES = Object.freeze([
  'prepared', 'snapshotted', 'database_compatible', 'switching_definitions', 'verifying',
  'pointer_switching', 'committed',
  'rolling_back', 'rolled_back', 'frozen',
]);

export async function deployHome23WorkerRuntime(input, deps) {
  if (input.processes.some((name) => !WORKER_RUNTIME_PROCESSES.includes(name))) throw new Error('unscoped PM2 target');
  if (input.addedProcesses.length || input.addedPorts.length) throw new Error('worker runtime must remain in owner harnesses');
  if (input.verifierCommand || input.verifierPath || input.restartCommand) {
    throw new Error('caller-supplied command is forbidden');
  }
  const release = await deps.release.verifyAndResolveManifest(input.releaseManifest, {
    requiredPatchIds: [input.homePatchId, input.websocketPatchId],
    stableStateRoot: '/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers',
    requireSafeRelativeCommandPaths: true,
    requireFullPayloadTreeHash: true,
    requireNoWritablePayloadPath: true,
    requireImmutableHome23Cli: true,
    requireImmutableGuardedPm2Save: true,
    requireImmutableKeychainHelper: true,
    forbidInMemoryKeychainInProduction: true,
  });
  const verifier = await deps.release.resolveVerifierProfile(release, input.verifierProfile);
  // resolveVerifierProfile returns the manifest-pinned Node path/hash, safe verifier path/hash,
  // and one exact frozen argv array. It accepts no caller argv or environment expansion.
  const admission = await deps.admission.classify({
    activePointer: input.activeReleasePointer,
    workerDatabase: input.workerDatabase,
    deploymentId: input.deploymentId,
  });
  let fence = null;
  if (admission.mode === 'first-deploy-bootstrap') {
    await deps.bootstrap.requireClosedFirstDeployProof({
      workerSchemaAbsent: true,
      ownerHarnessWorkerRuntimeDisabled: true,
      noActivePointer: true,
      noPriorDeploymentJournal: true,
      noGrantActivation: true,
      noCutoverState: true,
      noBillingAuthorizationOrSettlement: true,
      noLegacyWorkerConsequenceAuthority: true,
      preservationInventoryHash: input.preservationInventoryHash,
      requireCapabilitiesInactiveAfterBoot: true,
    });
  } else if (admission.mode === 'managed-redeploy') {
    const active = await deps.activeRelease.resolveProtectedChain(input.activeReleasePointer);
    await deps.activeRelease.requireExactAdmissionContext(active, admission.activeContext);
    fence = await deps.management.requireMaintenanceFence({
      subject: 'home23-runtime-deployment',
      receipt: input.maintenanceFenceReceipt,
      owningActionClass: 'home23-runtime-deploy',
      owningOperationId: input.deploymentId,
      blockedClasses: ['site', 'backend', 'stable-data', 'distribution', 'recovery', 'payment'],
    });
    await deps.management.requireNoPaymentSettlementDeploymentBlock();
  } else {
    throw new Error('deployment admission is neither closed bootstrap nor authenticated managed redeploy');
  }
  // Admission, command resolution, and release verification all finish before a journal, DB,
  // active-pointer, PM2, or process effect.
  await deps.pm2.assertCoherentHome(input.pm2Home);
  const lease = await deps.lease.acquireNew({ targetSet: input.processes, ttlMs: 30000 });
  const predecessorIdentity = await deps.runtime.readExactDefinitionsAndHashes(input.processes);
  // This is a read-only PM2/definition read. No restricted snapshot exists yet.
  const deployment = await deps.journal.prepareAndFsyncWithFence({
    deploymentId: input.deploymentId,
    releaseManifestPath: release.manifestPath,
    releaseManifestSha256: release.manifestSha256,
    candidateCodeRoot: release.codeRoot,
    candidateImplementationCommit: release.implementationCommit,
    candidatePayloadTreeSha256: release.payloadTreeSha256,
    home23CliPath: release.home23CliPath,
    home23CliSha256: release.home23CliSha256,
    guardedPm2SavePath: release.guardedPm2SavePath,
    guardedPm2SaveSha256: release.guardedPm2SaveSha256,
    keychainHelperPath: release.keychainHelperPath,
    keychainHelperSha256: release.keychainHelperSha256,
    predecessorIdentity,
    intendedPredecessorSnapshotPath: deps.runtime.restrictedSnapshotPath(
      input.restrictedRoot, input.deploymentId,
    ),
    generation: lease.generation,
    holderNonceHash: lease.nonceHash,
    orderedProcesses: input.processes,
    admissionMode: admission.mode,
    maintenanceFenceId: fence?.id ?? null,
    maintenanceFenceGeneration: fence?.generation ?? null,
    verifierExecutable: verifier.executablePath,
    verifierExecutableSha256: verifier.executableSha256,
    verifierPath: verifier.path,
    verifierSha256: verifier.sha256,
    verifierArgv: verifier.argv,
    verifierArgvSha256: verifier.argvSha256,
    state: 'prepared',
  });
  try {
    const predecessor = await deps.runtime.materializeRestrictedPredecessorSnapshotAndFsync({
      deploymentId: deployment.id,
      journalPath: deployment.path,
      expectedIdentity: predecessorIdentity,
      restrictedRoot: input.restrictedRoot,
      forbidOverwrite: true,
    }, lease);
    const predecessorReadback = await deps.runtime.readRestrictedPredecessorSnapshot(predecessor.path);
    await deps.runtime.assertSnapshotMatchesIdentityAndCurrentDefinitions(
      predecessorReadback, predecessorIdentity, input.processes,
    );
    await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'snapshotted', {
      predecessorSnapshotPath: predecessorReadback.path,
      predecessorSnapshotSha256: predecessorReadback.sha256,
      predecessorIdentitySha256: predecessorIdentity.sha256,
      fileAndParentDirectoryFsynced: true,
    });
    await deps.database.proveAndApplyForwardCompatibleMigration({
      liveDatabase: input.workerDatabase,
      predecessorRelease: predecessor.release,
      candidateRelease: input.releaseManifest,
      forbidStaleDatabaseRestore: true,
    });
    await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'database_compatible',
      await deps.database.compatibilityReceipt());
    for (const process of input.processes) {
      await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'switching_definitions', {
        process, phase: 'before', candidateDefinitionHash: release.processDefinitions[process],
      });
      await deps.runtime.startOrReloadExactDefinition(process, release, lease);
      const readback = await deps.runtime.readExactProcessIdentity(process);
      await deps.runtime.assertCandidateIdentity(readback, release);
      await deps.journal.appendProcessTransitionFenced(deployment, lease, { process, phase: 'after', readback });
      await deps.lease.renew(lease);
    }
    await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'verifying',
      await deps.runtime.readAllExact(input.processes));
    const verified = await deps.verifier.spawnExact({
      executable: verifier.executablePath,
      argv: [verifier.path, ...verifier.argv],
      expectedExecutableSha256: verifier.executableSha256,
      expectedScriptSha256: verifier.sha256,
      shell: false,
    });
    if (verified.status !== 'passed') throw new Error('live runtime verification failed');
    const intendedPointer = {
      path: input.activeReleasePointer,
      expectedPredecessorPointerHash: predecessor.activePointerSha256,
      deploymentJournalId: deployment.id,
      deploymentJournalPath: deployment.path,
      releaseManifestPath: release.manifestPath,
      releaseManifestSha256: release.manifestSha256,
      codeRoot: release.codeRoot,
      implementationCommit: release.implementationCommit,
      payloadTreeSha256: release.payloadTreeSha256,
      home23CliSha256: release.home23CliSha256,
      guardedPm2SaveSha256: release.guardedPm2SaveSha256,
      keychainHelperSha256: release.keychainHelperSha256,
    };
    await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'pointer_switching', {
      intendedPointer,
      verified,
    });
    const activePointerDraft = await deps.runtime.compareAndSwapActivePointerAndFsyncDirectory(
      intendedPointer, lease,
    );
    await deps.journal.appendPointerReadbackAndFsyncFenced(
      deployment, lease, activePointerDraft,
    );
    await deps.journal.transitionAndFsyncFenced(deployment, lease, 'committed', {
      committedManifestSha256: release.manifestSha256,
      committedCodeRoot: release.codeRoot,
      committedImplementationCommit: release.implementationCommit,
      committedPayloadTreeSha256: release.payloadTreeSha256,
      committedHome23CliSha256: release.home23CliSha256,
      committedGuardedPm2SaveSha256: release.guardedPm2SaveSha256,
      committedKeychainHelperSha256: release.keychainHelperSha256,
      activePointerSha256: activePointerDraft.sha256,
      verified,
    });
    const journal = await deps.journal.readCommittedAndVerifyFsync(deployment.id);
    const activePointer = await deps.activeRelease.resolveProtectedChain(input.activeReleasePointer);
    await deps.activeRelease.assertPointerJournalManifestReadback({ activePointer, journal, release });
    await deps.lease.release(lease);
    return {
      status: 'committed', admissionMode: admission.mode, predecessor, verified,
      deploymentId: deployment.id, activePointer, journal,
      verifierPath: verifier.path, verifierSha256: verifier.sha256,
      verifierArgv: verifier.argv, shell: false,
      fenceGeneration: fence?.generation ?? null,
    };
  } catch (error) {
    return rollbackDefinitionsFromJournalUsingSameDatabase(deployment, lease, error, deps);
  }
}

export async function handleDeploymentAtProcessStartup(processName, deps) {
  const deployment = await deps.journal.findNonterminalForTarget(processName);
  if (!deployment) return { disposition: 'none' };
  const live = await deps.lease.readLive(deployment.targetSet);
  if (live && live.generation === deployment.generation) {
    await deps.journal.appendStartupAckCas(deployment.id, deployment.generation, processName,
      await deps.runtime.readExactProcessIdentity(processName));
    return { disposition: 'joined_live_deployment' };
  }
  const recoveryLease = await deps.lease.claimExpiredByCas({
    deploymentId: deployment.id, expectedGeneration: deployment.generation,
  });
  if (!recoveryLease) return { disposition: 'another_reconciler_elected' };
  return reconcileOneDeploymentFenced(deployment, recoveryLease, deps);
}
```

Every effect uses deployment generation plus holder nonce as a fence and compare-and-swap expected state. The candidate pointer rename occurs only from the recorded predecessor pointer hash and already contains the deployment journal ID plus committed-manifest candidate hash. Until the subsequent `committed` journal transition is fsynced, the public active-release resolver deliberately fails closed; starting harnesses instead see the nonterminal lease/journal and join it. Deployment success is returned only after the committed journal and pointer are independently re-read through the protected chain and the full immutable tree/commands are revalidated. During a legitimate rolling reload, each starting process joins/acknowledges the live deploy lease and never initiates rollback. After orchestrator death and lease expiry, CLI/Jerry/Forrest race a single CAS; exactly one elected reconciler may finish verification or reload the exact predecessor definitions. `rollbackDefinitionsFromJournalUsingSameDatabase()` fsyncs `rolling_back`, reloads each recorded predecessor ecosystem definition with its exact entrypoint/cwd/args/env hashes, restores the predecessor informational pointer with an atomic rename plus directory fsync, and verifies health/readback before `rolled_back`. It never restores a stale SQLite copy.

The deploy API returns a closed discriminated receipt union. `committed` always includes `status`, `admissionMode`, `deploymentId`, `predecessor`, `verified`, fully read-back `activePointer`, fully read-back committed `journal`, `verifierPath`, `verifierSha256`, fixed `verifierArgv`, `shell: false`, and nullable `fenceGeneration`; `rolled_back` and `frozen` include the same deployment/command identity plus predecessor/rollback or urgent-recovery readbacks. A missing field, an in-memory pre-read object substituted for either readback, or a pointer/journal/hash disagreement fails the deploy test.

Worker SQLite and canonical manifests use forward-only additive migrations only after an exact predecessor/candidate compatibility suite proves: predecessor opens and writes the migrated copy; candidate sees predecessor writes; predecessor sees candidate writes to common contracts; new-only requests/receipts/authorizations remain intact across predecessor boot and later redeploy. Apply the migration transactionally with an online backup before new work resumes. A backup is usable only if migration itself fails before any post-migration write; after success, code rollback keeps the same live migrated database. If compatibility cannot be proven, deployment is blocked and must implement a versioned database pointer plus lossless post-snapshot event reconciliation instead.

Before prepare/deploy/save/reconcile, verify one coherent `PM2_HOME`: the pid-file PID, rpc/pub socket owners, daemon UID/start command/home, and every managed child must agree. The observed duplicate-God-daemon condition is a production blocker. `reconcile-pm2-home` is a separate journaled subcommand: under a global PM2-home lock it captures both daemons/sockets/children/dump, elects the daemon owning both sockets and all children, proves the other owns no socket/child, gracefully stops only that exact stale PID, atomically corrects the pid file, and re-verifies one daemon plus unchanged children. It never runs incidentally inside deploy and never kills an ambiguous daemon. Guarded PM2 save refuses incoherent state.

The deployment CLI has a closed tested subcommand/flag registry covering every later use: `prepare`, `pm2-home-status`, `reconcile-pm2-home`, `reconcile`, `admission-status`, `prepare-bootstrap-admission`, `deploy`, `verify-active`, `exercise-rollback`, and `restart-continuity`, including `--receipt-path-only` on the two terminal result producers. `admission-status` is the first operation after candidate/coherence validation, is read-only, atomically classifies open/frozen deployment state, and returns only `first-deploy-bootstrap`, `managed-redeploy`, `resume-existing-journal`, or `blocked`; no pre-admission mutating reconciliation is allowed. `prepare-bootstrap-admission` writes one content-addressed local receipt only after every closed first-deploy predicate passes and refuses if any management authority could exist. Tests extract later plan invocations, reject unknown flags, and exercise each subcommand. `rolled_back` verifies exact predecessor restoration, emits a retry-required receipt, and ends the Step 9 invocation; a fresh deployment requires a new Step 9 admission. `frozen` denies later deployment for the affected target set and writes an urgent Jerry-visible receipt with the exact recovery address. Neither terminal may enter candidate post-cutover verification.

require_safe_relative_file() {

home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")

          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

Expected: exactly one closed admission branch runs. Admission first writes a read-only content-addressed context: first/managed deployment returns the newly proposed ID only after proving no resumable journal exists, while recovery returns the authoritative existing journal ID/path and forbids a new journal. First deploy uses no unavailable Worker management call and leaves all live capabilities inactive; every later deploy verifies the exact active pointer chain, acquires the authenticated deployment-ID-bound fence, and rechecks the authoritative settlement block before its journal. Exactly the six named processes roll, no process definition or port is added, the returned typed receipt includes `deploymentId`, `activePointer`, committed `journal`, `verifierPath`, `verifierSha256`, fixed `verifierArgv`, and `shell: false`, and failure restores the predecessor pointer/process state automatically. The final immutable-verifier call records the content-addressed read-only Shakedown activation disposition consumed by Steps 10, 11, and 13.

- [ ] **Step 10: Install or converge ShakedownJerry through the deployed authenticated management plane**

Before any canonical Worker-state write, use the newly deployed service to refresh channels and automation/runtime inventory and require exact equality with the tracked Task 17 authorities; these commands are read-only and use `--no-write`. Any drift stops here and returns to Task 17 or Task 27, followed by a fresh Task 28/29 build and deployment. Classify activation as exactly `first_or_changed_hash` or `exact_same_release_and_grant_already_active`. The first requires live capabilities inactive. The second requires byte-identical release/profile/grant/target/network-policy hashes, the existing activation receipt, and the still-active exact Step 9 deployment fence; it preserves that exact activation and allows only no-op/repair-safe installation/readback while consequential dispatch remains blocked. A changed hash may never inherit activation, and an active-but-nonidentical state is a blocker.

On equality, install the exact template from `final_home_commit` idempotently into the stable Worker root while preserving the Task 16 source clone, state, runs, receipts, and activation records. Upsert the one resident pursuit and validate the installed profile under the classified disposition. For `first_or_changed_hash`, run a no-authority observe dry run. For `exact_same_release_and_grant_already_active`, run the same observation with live effects disabled by the deployment fence and prove the activation receipt/hash is unchanged. Write canonical install/upgrade, pursuit, inventory-readback, validation, and dry-run receipts. The Step 9 fence remains active through Task 29's restart/resurrection proof and is released only by Step 13 using the committed deployment receipt; Task 31 later acquires its separate deployment-epoch fence before its first consequence. A failed deploy or unresolved verification keeps the deployment fence held.

Before installing ShakedownJerry, complete the deferred migration of the six canonical installed workers `systems`, `freshness`, `memory`, `parity`, `release`, and `feeder`. The authenticated deployed handler resolves the canonical runtime and mode-`0700` preservation roots server-side, binds one mode-`0600` migration journal to the protected active pointer plus committed deployment journal/manifest, and performs each manifest replacement atomically. A real mutation creates exactly one content-addressed recovery copy and receipt before rename; the immediate second pass must report `no_change` and create neither. The handler proves every nonmanifest state/workspace/run/receipt byte unchanged. It then validates and executes one deployed read-only `post-migration-continuity` run for each worker. Any missing recovery receipt, partial migration, changed nonmanifest byte, replay drift, or failed real run leaves the deployment incomplete and its fence held. This is the production execution promised by Tasks 1 and 15, not another fixture rehearsal.

Install the exact Task 17 event-binding definition through the same authenticated plane while the worker is inactive or the Step 9 fence is active. The install is idempotent and stores exact definition/profile/grant hashes. A first install remains `active=0` with no activation epoch; an existing exact active binding retains its prior epoch only behind the fence. The trigger router cannot dispatch a binding until Task 31 atomically assigns the current applied cutover epoch. Hash-bound list readback is required here, again in Task 30, and after Task 31 activation.

From this point through Step 13, every fresh production shell begins by executing the entire literal active-release resolver from Step 3, copied byte-for-byte into each code fence before its defensive variable assertions. All Home23 verifier, management CLI, deployment/restart, and guarded-save calls use the exported immutable paths and Node executable; local test runners may still read committed test fixtures from the isolated worktree because they have no production mutation authority.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

A changed hash is always inactive.

- [ ] **Step 2: Present the exact grant summary and hash to the user**

Show allowed action classes and exact live targets, hard stops, configured accounts, budgets/rates, expiry/revocation behavior, rollback readiness, canonical grant hash, and current exact-hash activation status. If this is an inactive new hash, ask the user to activate that exact hash; prior general approval of the design or plan is not substituted. If a convergent rerun retained the already-active exact same hash, present the existing activation receipt and continue without manufacturing a second approval.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

- [ ] **Step 4: Prove activation, mismatch, revocation, and reactivation behavior**

Run one harmless covered read action without per-action approval. Attempt a modified-hash action and prove `require-human-authorization`. Then use the operator-only durable management-proof route: it journals the original exact activation and narrow fence before revoke, proves new live actions become authorization-required, reactivates only that recorded hash, and resumes safely after each failpoint. Separately prove a hard-denied target remains `deny`.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")

  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

}

Invoke `shakedown.code.integrate` for the exact Task 28 clone ref/commit. It creates a hash-bound run-scoped Git bundle, verifies and imports the previously independent objects through a temporary namespace, proves base/ancestry/patch identities, then atomically creates or updates only the dedicated canonical `refs/heads/codex/shakedown-worker/*` ref and removes the temporary ref. Prove the active operator checkout/remotes/index/worktree are unchanged and require the site/backend build commit to be reachable from that canonical ref. Materialize the exact immutable runner, frontend, backend, and operational release manifests from the canonical commit. A production cutover is blocked if its source is reachable only from the mutable worker clone or if any required object appeared without the verified import receipt.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

- [ ] **Step 4: Open one reentrant deployment epoch, fence all consequential ingress, and prove disabled replacement readiness**

Create or resume one `home23.shakedown-deployment-epoch.v1` journal that owns schedule/legacy-automation, stable-data, backend, frontend, Caddy/runtime, channel, and later proof transitions. Classify from one immutable snapshot as exactly `initial-cutover`, `already-applied-same-epoch`, `already-applied-upgrade`, `resume-applying-same-epoch`, or `retry-after-rolled-back-successor`. `already-applied-same-epoch` is legal only when the canonical cutover is `applied` and its final full-epoch completion transition binds the Step 7–10 proof hash; it branches before any baseline proof write, source integration, Worker enqueue, fence acquire/adopt/release, or other mutation and uses readback-only modes for all later rows. An interrupted `applying` record resumes from the exact first incomplete phase under its stored fence. A rolled-back predecessor is never reopened: retry creates a fresh nonce/recovery-receipt-bound successor. Initial cutover records full legacy definitions and absent/disabled replacement identities. Upgrade requires the two legacy automations to remain `PAUSED`, fences the current replacement schedules, keeps the same four schedule IDs, and records the prior replacement epoch—not legacy—as rollback target. An unknown mixed state stops before mutation.

Acquire the global deployment epoch lease plus billing/backend/site/data/collection/enrichment/distribution/recovery locks. Block new site/backend/data/distribution/recovery Worker actions and private billing-canary roots; read-only observation remains available. Wait for zero in-flight consequential Worker actions, collection/promoter writes, public/private Checkout Session creations, and signup mutation handlers. Stripe webhook ingress remains available only through its durable idempotent journal, while application of newly journaled webhook effects is held until the new backend is authoritative. Install or compare-and-swap all four replacement schedules disabled, rolling-restart the owner processes, and run the mapped missions in fixture/read-only shadow mode. Home23 cannot claim to fence a still-active Codex product scheduler. Before a real pre-pause canary, read each legacy automation's authoritative `nextRunAt`, require zero in-flight legacy execution, and require a no-due interval longer than the bounded canary deadline plus pause/readback margin. Monitor product state throughout and abort/enter reconciliation if any legacy start appears. Only inside that proven window, run one bounded manual replacement canary for each mapped logical role with distinct epoch-bound occurrence keys and shared consequence locks. Require a real end-to-end scan consequence and a real collection/enrichment consequence, disabled-schedule next-state projection, restart reconstruction, and authoritative receipts, then pause/read back both legacy definitions before the earliest next due. No prepared stable root or live pointer is written by a replacement schedule.

For an initial cutover only, only after both real manual replacement canaries and their restart/next-state proof, the execution agent performs fresh full-definition read -> exact-ID `automation_update` preserving every field but status -> authoritative readback for each exact legacy automation. Both must read `PAUSED`; a pre-read hash mismatch or uncertain product response leaves the epoch `reconciliation_required`. Upgrade/same-epoch paths never re-enable or rewrite legacy definitions. Append every canary, product, and scheduler readback to this same epoch.

runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

The public shadow dry run carries neither pursuit nor occurrence provenance. Its server resolver attaches the installed pursuit and the current cutover journal as a read-only source. The later `pre-pause-replacement-canary` mode derives its epoch-bound occurrence key only from that persisted cutover journal plus the installed schedule and enters through the internal scheduler-dispatch source resolver; no public `worker run` flag can inject either value.

For the exact initial-cutover operations receipt printed above, the executing Codex agent—not Home23 and not either verifier—now uses the automation product tool. It fresh-reads each of the two exact IDs, rejects a definition-hash mismatch, updates only `status` to `PAUSED` while preserving every other field, then performs authoritative product readback before the earliest recorded due time. The agent stores the tool results in the content-addressed product-readback input named by the operations receipt. Upgrade/retry/resume performs this external step only if that exact phase context still lists an unapplied product operation; an uncertain response stops with the deployment fence held. A fully applied same-epoch context performs no product call.

After that external product step, resume from durable state rather than shell variables:

set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

For Substack and each configured non-Substack public adapter, execute the smallest safe live canary and perform authoritative account/URL readback. Then exercise one safe update/correction on a canary artifact and obtain a distinct correction-handling/readback receipt. For consented communications, use one owned consented test recipient, prove suppression first with a suppressed fixture, send one bounded test communication, and obtain authoritative provider delivery/readback. Record that email is irreversible and never infer success from browser state alone.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

- [ ] **Step 9: Prove acquisition, indexing, social-image, mature campaign, and retirement consequences**

Ingest real search demand; load the deployed finalized discovery manifest and verify every route kind it reports eligible, while requiring the explicit unavailable-source receipt for lineage; complete one source-backed social-image repair or compliant asset improvement and verify live crawler-visible metadata/image; submit the complete changed canonical URL set through `shakedown.indexing`; and read back submission/index state without claiming indexing prematurely. Use an already mature attributable UTM campaign or wait through the actual configured maturity window. Completion requires joined UTM, behavior, and authoritative aggregate conversion evidence, a channel-score update, and retirement/revision of one weak recurring item. A future one-shot alone cannot pass this row.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

- [ ] **Step 10: Prove event exact-once, denial, rollback, restart, and lane isolation**

Deliver one safe live event twice and replay it, then prove exactly one request, one attempt, one canonical receipt, and one attached Shakedown pursuit consequence. Attempt one destructive website/data action and prove denial before effects. Force one channel adapter failure and prove observation, collection, and other lanes continue. That Worker action plan cannot revoke its own authority. After its receipt is terminal, use the operator-authenticated management CLI to revoke the exact standing-grant hash, prove new live work becomes authorization-required, and reactivate only that same hash; then use a read-only verifier to bind the action and operator-management receipt chains. Bind every restart/rollback receipt to the canonical source/release hashes. Finally, hash the complete data/backend/frontend/schedule/channel/distribution/acquisition/event proof set, append it to the still-open epoch, and call the authenticated cutover completion transition. A crash before that transition resumes `applying`; it never masquerades as an already-applied exact rerun.

runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

The verifier must enumerate every row and label only the payment canary `awaiting_separate_authorization`; it may not flatten that row into a full-system pass.

- [ ] **Step 12: Fence first, execute phase-aware recovery, then route the defect to its owner**

At the first failed boundary, fsync the failure and classify whether an epoch exists before dereferencing a cutover ID. A failure in Steps 1–3 uses `pre_epoch_no_consequence`: prove no schedule/product/data/backend/site consequence exists, reconcile the source-import journal independently, and write its owner handoff without inventing a cutover. For an existing epoch, acquire or retain the global consequence/payment/site/backend/data/collection/enrichment/distribution/recovery fence before any diagnosis, code edit, deploy, or further live action. Classify the global epoch phase and fresh authoritative state. If the state hash is exact and known, call authenticated `begin-rollback`, then authenticated `apply-local-recovery` for only the branded local operation rows. Before stable-data commit, the eligible product operations may restore the exact pre-epoch definitions. At or after stable-data commit, eligibility may restore only the prior replacement epoch or keep both ingress families paused; it must never restore a retired checkout-relative data pointer or re-enable a legacy writer against stable data. The executing Codex agent separately performs each eligible exact-ID automation product inverse through the product tool, with fresh hash precondition and full-definition preservation/readback. Home23 and the verifier never call that product API. Only after local and product readbacks are appended may fresh reconcile and `mark-rolled-back` run. Unknown drift, an uncertain product response, or a failed precondition remains fenced as `reconciliation_required`.

Only after `rolled_back`, or after a durable reconciliation-required handoff that leaves every consequence writer fenced, resume the exact earlier task that owns the module. Add the failing regression, implement and commit the root-cause repair there, rerun Task 28, redeploy Task 29, regenerate/reactivate the exact Task 30 grant hash if a bound hash changed, and restart Task 31 from Step 1. Do not patch live artifacts or create an ad hoc live-test commit.

      --operations-receipt-path-only \
      --service-url "$service_url" --credential-keychain-service home23.worker-management \
      --credential-account operator)
    local_recovery_receipt=$("$node_executable" "$home23_cli" worker automation-cutover apply-local-recovery shakedown-jerry \
      --cutover-id "$cutover_id" --operations-receipt "$rollback_operations" \
      --local-operations-only --receipt-path-only \
      --service-url "$service_url" --credential-keychain-service home23.worker-management \
      --credential-account operator)
    printf '%s\n' "$rollback_operations"
    ;;
  unknown-or-mixed)
    "$node_executable" "$home23_cli" worker automation-cutover reconcile shakedown-jerry \
      --cutover-id "$cutover_id" --fresh-authoritative-state \
      --require-status reconciliation_required --require-authoritative-readbacks \
      --service-url "$service_url" --credential-keychain-service home23.worker-management \
      --credential-account operator
    "$node_executable" "$shakedown_verifier" \
      --mode deployment-epoch-failure-recovery --cutover-id "$cutover_id" \
      --phase unknown-or-mixed --persist-reconciliation-required \
      --retain-all-consequence-fences --print-status
    "$node_executable" "$shakedown_verifier" --mode write-failed-boundary-handoff \
      --require-owner-task --require-failing-reproduction --forbid-live-patch \
      --require-rolled-back-or-fenced-reconciliation-required
    exit 0
    ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
```

If the printed rollback operations receipt contains eligible Codex product rows, the executing Codex agent now fresh-reads each exact automation ID through the product tool, validates its intended current hash, applies the full recorded eligible definition, and reads it back. The agent must omit every product row marked ineligible after stable-data commit. It stores the product-tool results at the content-addressed readback input named by the receipt. Any precondition mismatch or uncertain response stops here with all fences retained.

active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

Expected: credential provisioning yields one fresh validated private set and no secret output. The CLI derives operation validation from `BILLING_CANARY_OPERATIONS`, prompts for and records the exact live product/price, maximum charge, maximum net cost, and expiry, resolves all four private email/browser/payment/mailbox descriptors without exposing full values, computes their versioned HMAC binding set, and binds the stable Stripe API-version authority, specific fresh receipt, network policy/body schemas, mailbox target, Checkout host/callback set, public Auth confirmation set, cleanup-safety policy, validity ceilings, and private checkout/idempotency/session-journal contracts plus all immutable implementation hashes. The interactive-only summary pairs each fingerprint/version with operator-recognizable detail: masked email and mailbox account, browser profile label, and payment brand/last4/expiry. It is excluded from canonical receipts and never shows full addresses, paths, tokens, or payment data. Omission, expiry, overlong validity, insufficient execution/cleanup reserve, or drift of any binding fails before an unsigned request is written. It emits an unsigned exact request summary and hash; pause until the user authorizes every encoded bound.

- [ ] **Step 4: Sign, authenticate, register, and verify the exact approved hard-stop authorization**

Resume only after the user approves the exact canonical request hash shown in Step 3. Sign the document with the operator Keychain key, then call the authenticated operator-only registration endpoint with that same approved request hash and an immutable approval receipt. The server rehashes both unsigned scope and signed document, verifies signature/principal/expiry/bounds, records one active single-use authorization transactionally, and emits a redacted registration receipt. A different hash, stale expiry, absent authenticated approval receipt, non-operator credential, or standing-grant substitution writes no authorization row.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}

Expected: authoritative cleanup PASS from the Step 6 action journal, zero new side-effecting actions, pre-effect denial for an operation absent from the exact authorization, and a restart/reconstruction receipt proving the cleanup controller cannot duplicate an already terminal provider effect.

- [ ] **Step 8: Route any root-caused defect back through the tested billing implementation**

Stop the root at the failed boundary, preserve evidence, and revoke its main forward lane so no signup/checkout/charge can resume. Before editing code, deploying, or releasing the maintenance fence, the deterministic finalizer must classify authoritative provider state and terminalize the original hash:

- no mapped Checkout Session and no financial consequence: mark the armed safety lease `completed_no_consequence`, reconcile any uncertain started leaf, and skip every never-started forward/cleanup leaf with exact absence evidence;
- one mapped open Session and no charge: the cleanup controller alone runs `expire-session, cleanup`, verifies the Session cannot complete, then records `completed_via_safety`;
- an authoritative charge: the cleanup controller alone runs `cancel, refund, cleanup`, verifies exact cancellation/refund/detachment/no access/no renewal/net cost, then records `completed_via_safety`;
- any unknown/multiple provider identity or irreconcilable result: remain fenced in `reconciliation_required`; do not edit/redeploy and leave the durable safety controller as the only permitted writer.

For every terminalizable branch, reconcile started operations and skip never-started operations through the authenticated management API, restart the currently active immutable `jerry-api` while safety remains active, prove recovery produces zero duplicate effects, then close the authorization and prove replay denial. If signup consumed or may have consumed the email/password record, rotate the complete owned-email signup record to a new version under a separate exact interactive credential approval; invalidate the other ephemeral canary identity records as required by their schema. A retry always needs a newly prepared hard-stop document/hash over the new record set, even if code bytes are unchanged. No active hard-stop authorization or reusable identity may remain indefinitely.

Only after that terminalization receipt exists may implementation resume at Task 18: add the failing regression, fix both sides of any paired contract, stage only the declared source/tests, scan, commit, and repeat Tasks 28, 29, 30, and reentrant 31. Task 29's already-applied Supabase branch must remain read-only. Never repair production data around a code defect or redeploy around a live unresolved billing consequence.

set -euo pipefail
active_pointer=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime/active-home23-release.json
runtime_authority=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23/instances/workers/runtime
release_parent=/Users/jtr/_JTR23_/release/home23-code-releases/worker-runtime

json_raw() { /usr/bin/plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1"; }
sha256_file() { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'; }
require_owned_mode() {
  test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%u' "$1")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)"
  test "$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$1")" = "$2"
}
require_safe_relative_file() {
  relative_path=$1
  case "$relative_path" in ''|/*|*//*|./*|*/./*|../*|*/../*|*/..|.) return 1 ;; esac
  resolved_path=$(/bin/realpath "$active_code_root/$relative_path")
  case "$resolved_path" in "$active_code_root"/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  test -f "$resolved_path" && test ! -L "$resolved_path"
  printf '%s\n' "$resolved_path"
}
home23_tree_hash() {
  tree_root=$1
  (
    cd "$tree_root"
    LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/find . -mindepth 1 -print | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort |
      while IFS= read -r tree_path; do
        tree_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%Lp' "$tree_path")
        if test -L "$tree_path"; then
          tree_target=$(/usr/bin/readlink "$tree_path")
          tree_resolved=$(/bin/realpath "$tree_path")
          case "$tree_resolved" in "$tree_root"/*) ;; *) exit 91 ;; esac
          /usr/bin/printf 'l\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_target"
        elif test -f "$tree_path"; then
          tree_file_sha=$(/usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$tree_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
          /usr/bin/printf 'f\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path" "$tree_file_sha"
        elif test -d "$tree_path"; then
          /usr/bin/printf 'd\0%s\0%s\0' "$tree_mode" "$tree_path"
        else
          exit 92
        fi
      done
  ) | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
}
